items.title: Threatening to kill the President and his children is criminality, not free speech – Kwakye Ofosu
items.description: Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has described threats to kill President John Dramani Mahama and his children as “brazen criminality”, insisting that such conduct must not be defended in the name of free expression. Speaking on behalf of the President at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards in Accra, he urged political leaders not to support threats and incitement to violence for partisan advantage. “For instance, threatening to kill a president and his children is not free speech. It is brazen criminality. We, as political leaders, must not lend support to this level of criminality only because it enures to the benefits of our political fortunes,” he said. Mr Kwakye Ofosu said political leaders must demonstrate consistency in their defence of free speech, particularly when journalists face threats for publishing critical or uncomfortable reports. “Our words in support of free speech must not ring hollow, especially when in the north, in the past, journalists had to flee our country for fear of their lives because they published uncomfortable truths,” he stated. The Minister stressed that efforts to combat hate speech should not become a justification for restricting dissent, critical journalism or unpopular opinions. He said democracy depended on the freedom to disagree, but should not accommodate deliberate incitement of hatred, violence and intolerance. “Democracy thrives on disagreement, and what it cannot accommodate is the deliberate incitement of hatred, violence, and intolerance. A clear distinction must be struck between criminal conduct and the expression of free speech,” he said. The comments were made at the 30th GJA Media Awards, held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Advancing Media Freedom and Combating Hate Speech in the Digital Age.” The event brought together journalists, media organisations and other stakeholders to recognise excellence in journalism and discuss issues affecting media freedom.

items.title: A DECADE OF ROYAL SPLENDOUR: Oba Ewuare II’s 10th coronation anniversary
items.description: By Moses Stowe There are moments in the history of a people when the past and the present meet in a compelling celebration of identity, pride and continuity. For the people of the ancient Benin Kingdom, the 10th Coronation Anniversary of His Royal Majesty, Omo N’Oba N’Edo Uku Akpolokpolo, Ewuare II, CFR, the Oba of Benin, represents one such moment. A decade after ascending the revered throne, the monarch’s anniversary provides an opportunity to celebrate the enduring institution of the Benin monarchy, reflect on its contributions to cultural preservation and reaffirm the values that have sustained the kingdom across generations. More than a ceremonial commemoration, the anniversary brings together culture, history, sports, intellectual discourse, community engagement and royal pageantry in a programme designed to showcase the richness of Benin heritage. For Eagle Aromatic Schnapps, Nigeria’s Authentic Traditional Prayer Drink, culture is more than a reflection of the past; it is a living heritage that connects generations, reinforces communal identity and preserves the values that define a people. This belief finds meaningful expression in the 10th Coronation Anniversary of His Royal Majesty, Oba Ewuare II, CFR, the Oba of Benin Kingdom. As a brand whose identity is rooted in Nigeria’s traditional heritage, Eagle Aromatic Schnapps recognises the significance of royal institutions as custodians of history, customs and cultural continuity. Its association with this historic milestone reflects the brand’s appreciation of the traditions that have sustained the Benin Kingdom and contributed to Nigeria’s diverse cultural identity. Eagle Aromatic Schnapps identifying with the anniversary goes beyond participating in a royal celebration. It represents an opportunity to reaffirm the importance of cultural preservation, community engagement and respect for the traditional institutions that continue to shape the country’s social fabric. Speaking on the significance of the anniversary, John Bamgbose, Assistant Brand Manager, Schnapps and Gin, Intercontinental Distillers Limited, described the occasion as an opportunity to celebrate the Benin Kingdom’s rich history and the values that connect generations. He said, The 10th Coronation Anniversary of His Royal Majesty, Omo N’Oba N’Edo Uku Akpolokpolo, Ewuare II, CFR, is a remarkable milestone in the history of the Benin Kingdom. It is a celebration of royal heritage, cultural identity, continuity and the enduring spirit of a people whose history has made a lasting contribution to Nigeria’s national identity. At Eagle Aromatic Schnapps, we recognise that our cultural heritage is one of our greatest treasures. Our traditions tell our stories, connect generations and remind us of the values that make our communities unique. When we celebrate our traditional institutions, we are also celebrating the history, creativity and collective identity of the people they represent. We are delighted to identify with this historic milestone and celebrate the Benin Kingdom as it marks ten years of the reign of His Royal Majesty. We recognise the importance of preserving our cultural heritage and creating opportunities for younger generations to understand and appreciate the traditions that have shaped our society. For Eagle, cultural engagement is about recognising what connects us as a people. It is about respecting our traditions, valuing our communities and supporting meaningful occasions that keep our heritage alive. We believe that when culture is preserved and appreciated, it becomes a bridge between our past, our present and our future. Bamgbose added that the brand values meaningful engagement with Nigeria’s cultural institutions and communities, recognising the importance of responsible corporate participation in traditional celebrations. The anniversary programme, scheduled throughout October 2026, reflected these values through a rich blend of cultural displays, royal pageantry, sporting competitions, intellectual engagements and community-focused activities. From the Cultural Festival, to the Food Festival, Art Exhibition and Trade Fair, to the Wrestling Competition, to the Oba Erediauwa Memorial Lecture, to football match to the Durbar the programme presents multiple opportunities to celebrate the heritage, creativity and collective identity of the Benin people. According to the Obasogie of Benin Kingdom: The significance of the Oba of Benin’s 10th Coronation Anniversary extends beyond the marking of ten years on the throne. It lies in the opportunity to renew appreciation for an institution that embodies the history, identity and cultural continuity of the Benin people. The anniversary programme brings different dimensions of society into one celebratory framework, demonstrating how tradition can remain relevant while creating space for contemporary interests and future aspirations. As the people of the Benin Kingdom celebrate this royal milestone, the broader lesson is that heritage thrives when it is understood, valued and passed on. Traditional institutions preserve the memories of generations, communities keep their customs alive, and responsible corporate engagement can contribute to a wider appreciation of the cultural identities that define the nation. The Grand Reception on October 20, 2026, provided a fitting climax to the 10th Coronation Anniversary celebrations, attracting an impressive gathering of dignitaries, political leaders and distinguished guests. The occasion was graced by the Governor of Edo State, the Deputy Governor, members of the State Executive Council, including Commissioners, and other prominent personalities who joined the Benin Kingdom in honouring His Royal Majesty, Omo N’Oba N’Edo Uku Akpolokpolo, Ewuare II, CFR. The gathering reflected the significance of the Benin monarchy as a symbol of cultural heritage, unity and traditional leadership, while further underscoring the importance of the historic milestone. For Eagle Aromatic Schnapps, the occasion provided another opportunity to celebrate the enduring relationship between Nigeria’s cultural institutions, community identity and the traditions that unite generations. For Eagle Aromatic Schnapps, these celebrations reinforce a simple but powerful message: when we celebrate our traditions, we preserve our identity; when we honour our cultural institutions, we strengthen the connections that bind generations together. Also, cultural heritage remains one of Nigeria’s most valuable assets, deserving recognition, respect and preservation. By identifying with significant traditional occasions, the brand seeks to reinforce the importance of the customs, institutions and communities that continue to shape the nation’s cultural identity. Ultimately, the 10th Coronation Anniversary is more than a commemoration of a decade on the throne. It is a celebration of continuity, collective pride and the enduring connection between a people and their heritage. As the Benin Kingdom honours its past and looks towards the future, Eagle Aromatic Schnapps celebrates alongside the wider appreciation of Nigeria’s rich cultural traditions. items.title: 2027: Danladi vows to build on AbdulRazaq’s achievements
items.description: By Demola Akinyemi ILORIN – The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kwara State, Rt. Hon. Salihu-Yakubu Danladi, has said his seven years of experience in the legislature and familiarity with the state’s development challenges have prepared him to govern the state. Danladi, who is also the Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly, pledged to consolidate the achievements of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq and take the state to greater heights if elected in the 2027 governorship election. He said Kwara needed continuity and further development rather than a return to what he described as its ugly past. The APC candidate spoke during the News Keg, an interactive programme organised by the Kwara State Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), where he discussed his political journey, legislative experience, achievements and development agenda ahead of the 2027 election. Danladi maintained that he was not a political novice, having served as Speaker since 2019 and participated in legislative processes supporting the present administration’s programmes. “I am not new to what is happening in Kwara State today. I have spent seven years in the legislature. No other candidate had any experience in government. I know virtually every sector and the challenges confronting the state,” he said. He argued that his legislative experience had given him a broad understanding of governance, particularly through the House of Assembly’s appropriation and oversight responsibilities, which he said complemented the executive’s implementation of policies and projects. The governorship candidate, an electrical engineering graduate, also highlighted his academic pursuits, disclosing that he had undertaken programmes in revenue management, peace, conflict and security studies and was currently pursuing a PhD in economic development. Reflecting on his representation of Ilesha/Gwanara Constituency, Danladi identified access to potable water, rural roads, healthcare, education and security as some of the major challenges that informed his legislative interventions. He said he facilitated the provision of about 210 boreholes across communities in his constituency during his first term, alongside the construction and rehabilitation of rural roads. One of the projects he highlighted was a 33-kilometre road linking communities in the constituency, which he said had significantly improved movement in the area. According to him, residents previously endured several hours of travelling during the rainy season for journeys that would ordinarily take about 30 minutes. On healthcare, the Speaker said he facilitated interventions in 18 primary healthcare centres and supported efforts to improve existing general and cottage hospitals. He added that his interventions had extended beyond his constituency, noting that his position as Speaker had provided opportunities to support development projects and empowerment programmes in other parts of the state. Addressing insecurity, particularly in Kwara North, Danladi said he facilitated the training of 300 local security personnel to strengthen surveillance and intelligence gathering in vulnerable communities, especially border settlements in Baruten Local Government Area. He described security as fundamental to development and called for sustained collaboration among security agencies, traditional rulers, community leaders and local authorities. On his proposed administration’s priorities, the APC candidate listed human capital development, agriculture, electricity and rural infrastructure as key areas of focus. He said improved road networks connecting farming communities to urban markets would reduce transportation costs, increase farmers’ earnings and contribute to lower food prices. Danladi also lamented electricity challenges confronting several rural communities in Baruten, but said partnerships with investors had facilitated alternative power arrangements, including solar-powered electricity in some settlements. He identified the establishment of the Federal Science and Technical College in Kwara North as another important intervention capable of expanding educational opportunities and stimulating development in the district. On the political debate surrounding calls to rescue Kwara, the APC candidate questioned the rationale behind such demands, arguing that the state should focus on consolidating its development efforts. “Why are some people saying they want to rescue Kwara? Is it from the infrastructure and development that are going on, or do we want to move forward? In life, there is no limit to development. We must continue to move forward,” he said. He described AbdulRazaq as a leader who had laid a foundation for the state’s development, pledging to sustain ongoing programmes and improve on existing achievements. “My brother has laid a good foundation for Kwara, and the next step is for us to build on that foundation. I am part and parcel of the foundation. It will therefore be easier for us to consolidate the gains already recorded,” he said. Danladi also pledged balanced development across the three senatorial districts, assuring residents of Kwara North, Central and South that none would be neglected under his administration. He expressed optimism about the economic potential of Kwara North, particularly in agriculture, rural infrastructure and electricity, saying strategic investments in the areas would stimulate economic activities and discourage rural-urban migration. The News Keg initiative is part of the Correspondents’ Chapel’s efforts to promote issue-based political discourse and accountability by providing voters with opportunities to assess the policies, experience and development plans of candidates seeking to govern the state in 2027. items.title: Birthday greetings to my Oba of Lagos, by Dele Sobowale
items.description: “It is the part of a king to do good to his subjects and be maligned for it” – Alexander the Great, 356-323 BC, King of Macedonia. Seldom does this column write about our Royal Fathers. Today, two of them are the focus of attention – for the best of reasons. His Imperial Majesty Alayeluwa Oba Rilwanu Babatunde Osuolale Aremu Akiolu I, CFR, who, unknown to many people, is a lawyer, Fellow of the Nigerian Law School, Member of the Nigerian Institute of Management, Oba of Lagos and Permanent Chairman, Lagos State Council of Obas and Chiefs, celebrated another birthday last week. This article should have been published then. But, the commitment to publish a tribute to Chief Kesington Adebutu, GCON, FNIJ, the day after his 91st birthday on October 24, 2026, was made months before last week. And, it is never my style to treat eminent individuals in society with levity. I have two other reasons to prostrate before my Royal Father. First, unknown to Baba, I am his in-law. My wife was the last daughter of Chief Imam Isiaka Shittu, the left full back of the first Nigerian football team to play in Britain; her mother was an elder sibling to Kabiyesi. I was an active cheerleader during his contest for the stool; and celebrated extensively when he ascended the throne of his forefathers. I pray for him daily. “Governing Italians is not impossible; it is merely useless” – Benito Mussolini, 1883-1945, Italian Fascist leader. “Italians are rascals the world over” – Leopold Mozart, 1719-1781. Second, the Lagos Island Oba Rilwanu Akiolu I inherited could have been aptly described with the same words Mussolini and Mozart used to portray Italians. I was born on the Island in 1944; and very familiar with every single square inch of it. At the risk of being accused of denigrating the contributions of Oba Rilwanu’s predecessors, I strongly believe that their professions before becoming the monarch strongly influenced their leadership style. His immediate past predecessor, Oba Adeyimika Oyekan II, despite a short stint in the British Army during World War II, was a pharmacist. He served in the Medical Corps; not a combatant soldier. By contrast, Oba Osuolale was a police officer for years and rose to the rank of Assistant Inspector General before retiring. Discipline came as second nature to him. Right from the start, he set out to instill order into Isale-Eko where the Iduganran Palace is situated. Today, the area characterized by filth and lawlessness has been transformed. Where none but the brave and armed could venture after dark, Isale-Eko is now safer than most parts of Nigeria after dark. A lot more can be written about how the Oba stamped his authority on the Island. Expectedly, he was maligned for it. Rumour-mongers portrayed him as ruthless and distant from people – including his family members. The title ‘Olowo-Eko’, Lagos rich man, was frequently not uttered as a compliment. I reserved judgment. Then, something happened recently which will remain indelible in my mind for ever. OBA AS GOOD SAMARITAN “No one would remember the Good Samaritan, if he only had good intentions” – Lady Margaret Thatcher, British Prime Minister. One of Kabiyesi’s cousins, name withheld, had a life-threatening health crisis requiring very urgent attention. Rushed to the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH, by other cousins, it seemed as if the end had come. The hospital requested for deposit running to eight figures. A meeting was held quickly; and it was clear that the entire extended family could not raise the money so quickly to save her life. Despair set in. But Miguel de Unamuno had said: “It is despair and despair alone, that begets heroic hope, absurd hope, mad hope.” Out of desperation, one of the care-givers offered a suggestion. “Why not ask Oba Akiolu for help?” Long silence followed. With no other option left; and with little hope of success, a delegation was sent to the Palace. Miracles still happen to those who believe in them. In less time than it has taken you to read this article, Oba Akiolu I had sent the funds needed to LASUTH; he sent more money later. Suddenly, the tune has changed. Nobody sent me on this errand; but, as one of the care-givers to the patient, I am in the best position to publicly acknowledge the generosity of our Royal Father on this occasion. I mentioned the gesture to one of my close associates, very close to the Palace; and I discovered that this was not the first time Kabiyesi would help people in distress. Now, I have my own opinion of our caring Father which can never be erased. Almighty Allah will grant our Royal Father longer life and increasing prosperity. Happy birthday Baba. I prostrate full length. P.S. Oba Akiolu I will celebrate two anniversaries next year. He will be celebrating 24 years on the throne; and on October 29, 2027, Alayeluwa will be 84 years young. Somebody should produce a chronicle of those glorious years – particularly including the latest revelations about a totally misunderstood but caring Father of his people. NIGERIA’S CASH AND CARRY JUDICIARY – 1 “It is very well to paint justice blind; but, she does better without a bandage round her eyes. She should indeed be blind to favour and prejudice, but, clear to which way lies the truth” – British Jurist, Lord Denning, 1899-1999 Once upon a time, it seems so long ago now, Nigerian Justices were south as Chief Justices of other African nations. Three Nigerians – Dr Elias, Udoma Udo Udoma and Prince Ajibola – served meritoriously in the World Court. Today, no country or institution takes a glance at Nigeria; when in search of a jurist to settle any matter – criminal or civil. Our judiciary has acquired a well-deserved notoriety for alleged misconduct, no party to any litigation would trust the court to be impartial – if there is a Nigerian jurist sitting on it. Since “charity begins at home”, it is not surprising that the travesty of justice was home grown – Made in Nigeria. For a long time, the National Judicial Council, NJC, has challenged critics to prove the allegations. There has been no proof – until now. An insider, retired Justice of the Supreme Court, Amina Augie, at the 40th anniversary of the Nigerian Law School Class of 1986, declared that corruption has transformed “the one place that a citizen should find impartiality into one more market stall” – that is a kiosk or shed in market place language. Nigerian justice has become transactional. Retired Justice Augie has flipped the script. As a long term insider, she must have experienced the rot first hand; must have been tempted several times by litigants – some of whose lawyers were in attendance at the lecture. Only God knows how many Senior Advocates of Nigeria, SANs, have been made; not because their brilliance or the justice of their cases, but because they knew how to grease the palms of perverted court Registrars working hand-in-glove with conscienceless Justices. Court Orders Arrest, Detention of NURTW Leader – Sahara Reporters. I was in my area when the news broke. Several young men familiar with the judiciary were present. To my question: “Will the NURTW leader be arrested and detained?” The answer was unanimous. The Justice is wasting his time. The Police will never arrest the suspect and that will be the end of the matter. That summarises the contempt Area Boys have for the Nigerian Police and judiciary. P.S: The report of the NURTW leader’s arrest and detention ordered by a Justice was published three days ago. Unconfirmed information indicates that the order has not been carried out. Meanwhile, Area Boys and girls continue to share video showing the “untouchable”, surrounded by women of easy virtue, without fear of apprehension. With those well-connected, the judiciary can bark; but it cannot bite. This is the first part of a longer article slated for the near future. I want to close by asking three questions. How many Nigerians, when in court, feel absolutely certain that justice would be done at the end of the trial – win or lose? Corrupt Justices don’t act alone; and they seldom pervert justice without the collaboration of lawyers and other people. Do the collaborators feel a sense of remorse after the judgment is delivered embalming injustice? There is a big one for politicians contesting the 2027 elections. Will you go to court if you lose and why? From all indications, it might make more sense to walk into a den of robbers in the dark than go to court after being declared loser by INEC. ALL ROADS LEAD TO OLOMU KINGDOM NOVEMBER 15, 2026 – 2 “Aye, every inch a King” – William Shakespeare, 1564-1616 The Olomu of Olomu Kingdom, Albert Akpomudje, SAN, FCIArb, sits atop three monumental institutions simultaneously. Most people would feel eminently fulfilled to be the President Worldwide of a great secondary school like Government College, Ughelli; the school which has produced several eminent Nigerians. He is now the 54th Chairman, Body of Benchers – the topmost position in the Nigerian Bar. Finally, he is now the OHWORODE OF OLOMU KINGDOM, DELTA STATE. Next Sunday, the Ohworode of Olomu Kingdom will celebrate his birthday and first coronation as His Royal Majesty. Follow me on Facebook @ J Israel Biola The post Birthday greetings to my Oba of Lagos, by Dele Sobowale appeared first on Vanguard News .

Kébémer : le bilan du présumé naufrage d’une pirogue passe à 21 morts
items.description: Le bilan du présumé naufrage d’une pirogue transportant des candidats à l’émigration irrégulière s’est alourdi, passant de quatre à 21 morts. Ce samedi, les côtes de Loumpoul, dans le département de Kébémer, offrent un spectacle particulièrement macabre. Les corps sans vie sont alignés les uns à côté des autres sur la rive. Les éléments de la gendarmerie et les sapeurs-pompiers poursuivent les opérations de recherche, dans l’espoir de retrouver d’autres victimes. Selon notre source, la plupart des victimes seraient originaires des communes de Léona et de Thiéppe. Cette tragédie plonge les populations dans l’émoi et la consternation. Pour l’heure, les dépouilles sont acheminées vers le district sanitaire de Kébémer. Ces derniers temps, le phénomène de l’émigration irrégulière, avec son lot de conséquences tragiques, prend de plus en plus d’ampleur. Face à cette problématique persistante, il devient urgent de trouver des solutions durables pour endiguer ce fléau. Falel Pam

items.title: You need to move on by forgiving that affair
items.description: By Bunmi Sofola Someone once dubbed Lagos the adultery capital of the world. A bit unfair judging by the frantic global bed-hoppingsthat go on all over the place. But it does not mean that adultery is no longer the shocker it used to be. So can you forgive a straying partner? Joy, a top executive in the marketing department of a manufacturing company, said she’d invested so much into her relationship over eight years to let a little thing like adultery destroy it. “Call it the seven-year itch”, said Joy, “but we’d been living together for that long when Afe, my partner’s affection, began sliding. “It was the little things that stopped first, like his afternoon phone calls saying he was thinking of me. He started going out more with his male friends, but as they were mine too, I trusted them to keep him in line. Then he started going out to work functions but when I asked why, we’d end up arguing and he would charge out of the house, then, this fateful day, I’d been away for an advert shooting for my company for a couple of day and when I returned home, the photographs of us that sat on top of the television had gone. “Afe said he thought I’d taken it with me, but it turned up two days later back on the television set. Afe said he’d forgotten he’d taken it to the office to show someone. But I know most of his work colleagues, so why bother to take in a picture of us? A few weeks later, he forgot his cheque book at home and I was concerned at the amount of money he’d been withdrawing. I went to his office to confront him. It was a few weeks to Christmas and I read the cards on his desk while waiting for him. One read: “Darling, sorry we won’t be spending Christmas together but you’ll be in my thoughts all day. Wish you could be here with me. All my love, you cuddly teddy bear”. When I threw the card in Afe’s face, he had the grace to look shame-faced. The girl in question turned out to be a colleague, but it had been going on for months He said on the few occasions I’d gone out of town on advert shoots, he’d felt neglected and this girl had offered a shoulder to cry on. Without letting him know, I met up with this girl and she confessed she’d been to the flat. She also said Afe had made it clear she was only a fling and she was having none of that. “My self confidence really took a nose-dive and I even thought of calling off the whole thing. But I loved Afe – we had lasted seven years – longer than many marriages and I wasn’t prepared to throw it all away. Another Christmas is around the corner, there are days when I wonder what he gets up to at work and the women he socializes with, but I know he wouldn’t jeopardise my love. Come Christmas, I’m expecting him to make up for the heartache he caused me last year …” Florence’s partner cheated on her with an ex-girlfriend. “I knew Bobson saw his girlfriend from time to time”, said Florence. “They had been together for some five years and had mutual friends before they decided to go their separate ways. But it never worried me because he always joked about her behind her back, so I assumed there was just a lot of ill feelings between them. Bobson was two years younger than me, but I tended to attract younger men, when we were introduced through mutual friends at a dinner party, we clicked right away. “We didn’t actually live together, but we stayed with each other five nights a week and I believed he didn’t need anyone else. He was always generous and affectionate and we had a healthy sex life. He was fairly successful car dealer, so I know how charming he could be and that other women found him attractive, but never had reason to doubt him. So I’ll never forget the shock of the discovery that he was cheating. We had a lot of drink after a lovely meal at his flat and were having a cuddle when he whispered, I have that liquor you liked so much in the bedroom. We could have that upstairs if you like – like the last time. Reality hit me, whoever he’d enjoyed the liquor with, it certainly hadn’t been with me. He tried to bluff his way out of it but when I had a go at hi, he admitted he had been seeing his ex-girlfriend for months now. The jokes had used to crack about her had been a cover-up. He said he still loved her and he never had the strength to turn her away. I realized how conceited and weak he was. I was convinced I didn’t do anything to push him into having an affair. But it didn’t matter how great our relationship was – one woman was never going to keep him happy. He begged me for another chance and I tried to make a go of it, but the trust had gone. I knew I had to start all over again with someone else. I would only have myself to blame if I married him knowing he was a cheat. Immaculate Conception (Humour) A mother took her daughter to the doctor’s. “She’s been having strtange symptoms”, said the mother. The doctor examined the daughter carefully. Then he announced. “Madam, I believe your daughter’s pregnant”. “That’s impossible”, the mother gasped. “Why, my little girl has nothing whatsoever to do with men, do you darling? No, mummy, I’ve never so much as kissed a man”. The doctor then looked from mother to daughter. Then he walked to the window and stood there, staring out. Finally, the mother asked: “Doctor, something wrong?” “No”, he replied. “It’s just that the last time anything like this happened, a star appeared in the East, so I was looking to see if there was another one”. Mind Your Language (Humour) A virile young Italian soldier is relaxing in his favourite bar in Rome, when he attracts a gorgeous, young blonde. They go back to his apartment and make love. Afterwards, the soldier says with a smile,” you finish?” She frown and replies: “No. Surprised, the young man reaches for the beautiful girl … and the love making resumes. She seems to enjoy herself. As the love making ends, the solder asks smugly: “This time, you finish?” She returns his smile and whispers contentedly: “No”. Puzzled out determined, he reached for her again. They make love once again until the exhausted man falls back, gasping. Barely able to turn his head, he asks: “So you finish?” “No!” She shouts back. “Stop asking I now finish. I sweedish”. The post You need to move on by forgiving that affair appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigeria’s unique political campaigns, by Tonnie Iredia
items.description: To strengthen the growing trend of dialogue over disputes and wars, the United Nations Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) declared the 1970s as the decade of communication. The expectation was that every country would endeavour to become a communicating nation. Not many have successfully embraced the appeal till today because everyone has adopted a haphazard approach to the subject. Government, societal institutions and the general public have continued to relate with themselves and one another through the ‘transmission model’ which sees communication not as an exchange of ideas but as the mere transmission of messages with or without a purpose. In other words, once a message is transmitted, it does not matter whether the receiver understands it or not. The unavoidable consequence of the approach is that communication has largely remained ineffective. The commonest of the phenomenon is the communication that is often swallowed by noise. Nothing else better exemplifies this point than the current electioneering campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections where all that is heard is noise within and among large crowds. All our political parties appear convinced that the best way to address the masses is to demonstrate capacity to put together large crowds that are engaged in the communication of the deaf. Many people among the crowd are in attendance with different goals in mind just as many do not in essence understand the purpose of the gathering. The trend is fast becoming Nigeria’s unique contribution to the development of democracy. In fairness to our political class, several theories of mass mobilization and information flow are put in use in the campaigns across the country. The missing point is that no one knows whether the communication theories as currently practiced add any value to the comprehension of the political messages that are being disseminated. A common scheme is the two-step flow model which posits that the media influences the public indirectly through opinion leaders, who interpret and relay information to others. In line with this model, politicians seek to use revered leaders to pass messages to the people in addition to what the media does. The problem here is that not many people are willing to listen to some of the so-called leaders because the latter are no longer regarded as credible by the people. The case of traditional rulers for instance has virtually become a double-edge sword because they are now seen as enemies of the opponents of their preferred candidates. Such traditional rulers are generally being robbed of the title of the people’s royal fathers that are expected to be non-partisan. This has encouraged campaign coordinators to expand to the multiple-step flow theory. In today’s Nigeria, the steps are greatly affected by the prevailing socio-economic factors in the environment. When an international music or soccer star is introduced into a political rally, the strategy pulls a huge crowd but do the people get to hear whatever is being said? This is difficult to determine when it is realized that the same huge crowd surfaces the next day when the event is organized by another political party. Accordingly, it is getting increasingly difficult to evaluate the real support which a large crowd adds to the fortunes of each campaign team. It is however not in doubt that everyone probably gets entertained and perhaps finds some material gains before leaving making it obvious that campaigns are now sources of economic gains to many spectators. Another strategy remains the use of the media by strong advocates who engage in interviews to sell the candidates of their parties. Here, the television networks have had a field day. Unfortunately, it has not added much value to the campaigns because most of the advocates approach the task with a fruitless mindset. A television interview which is ordinarily a great opportunity for a party chieftain is marred as most party representatives seek to change the interview format to what in political broadcast is known as ‘party talk.’ In the latter, the party representative gets a free no-interruption opportunity to say whatever he likes. But the situation changes when it is an interview. Here, questions would be asked, follow-ups would be done and indeed, interruptions will occur where critical terms are referred to while answering questions. The trend one sees now is that the party official demands not to be interrupted while answering questions. The other week, a party official said publicly that he came prepared to face the interviewer! The professional position is that the interviewer represents the general public as his questions are generally crafted in line with comments in the public space. The guest is therefore expected to see his interviewer not as a particular person but as a typical citizen whose views he ought to respond to with a mind to changing or reducing to the barest minimum, any anxieties real or imagined that citizens hold against his party. Indeed, a party official at a public interview session is admonished to ignore the nuances of his interviewer and deal with the substance of the message in favour of his political party. To go for a television interview with a mindset to deal with a naughty interviewer is patently ill-advisable. Sadly, that is what we see these days on national television in Nigeria with a politician seeking to take control of a programme in which he is only a guest. Even if a combative approach such as aggressively demanding respect from an interviewer was what the party had planned, it is wise to realize that the posture cannot explain to the public why the party is asking for our votes. To drive home the point, let me recall my personal experience as an interviewer with President Shehu Shagari seeking re-election in 1983. I asked Shagari if I was free to describe him as ‘the happy leader’ of corrupt politicians since Nigerians see his party the NPN as a collection of money bags and thieves. While answering me, he said his smiles increased because he saw me displaying brilliance by playing the devil’s advocate of deliberately projecting an erroneous opinion. He admitted that the NPN may have some bad eggs as it is with all organizations but that because it was larger than all others in everything it also has the largest number of honest hardworking Nigerians. He regretted that it was because the media likes to focus on negatives that it was magnifying NPN’s few bad eggs. He then listed all the popular programmes that the NPN had implemented that should interest Nigerians instead of fake propaganda by political opponents. If that type of question is asked today not only by the NTA but also by the private media, our law enforcement agencies would be on 24hours red alert. The scenario outside the television studios does not also show that political campaigns in Nigeria follow what happens elsewhere. Whether it is the ruling party that everyone is complaining about or the opposition parties that are preoccupied with complaints, almost every political campaign is violent. There are politicians who are experts in issuing threats while others are engaged in unorthodox practices that make it impossible for anyone to hear the message of any campaign. All parties as stated earlier, are busy creating crowds with noise. Anyone who thinks it is the APC alone that is busy renting crowds should check out for what the ADC did last week in parts of Northern Nigeria. Media reports indicate that because the ADC shut down the relevant towns, those who flew to the rallies were yet to find space to drive from the airport to the rally venues when it was time for their return flight to depart. In other parts of the country the goal was really to just create crowd and entertain people, not really to educate Nigerians on why they should vote for whom. In Bayelsa state, the home of the NDC leader, the communication of campaign messages took the form of a boat regatta. In some other states it was violence galore with thugs destroying campaign materials of other political parties in addition to state authorities disallowing the use of public media and spaces like stadia. The reported attack on Vice President Shettima’s entourage in Lafia is instructive here. In other words, we are still not ready for the politics of equality featuring a level playing field. A foreign journalist visiting Nigeria would wonder if we detest peace communication until he finds out that we actually have a national peace committee. Whereas many believe that the situation could produce an avalanche of electoral disputes, the judiciary is likely to use technicalities to deal with the development if history is allowed to remind us of the past. Put differently, the judiciary may once again be more active than our electoral body in the conduct of elections in Nigeria. The post Nigeria’s unique political campaigns, by Tonnie Iredia appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Receive what you confess, by Funmi Komolafe
items.description: Gradually, year 2026 is drawing to an end. Being alive is a reason we must continuously thank God. Brethren, have you said thank you Jesus this morning? Please do. You owe the Lord gratitude. Beloved, last week we mentioned confession as a key to a miracle. Today, we’ll return to that with more details. I’ll start with an uncommon story of the son of a farmer whose father was regarded as poor in a town. This young boy went to the farm with his father and he saw man drive past them in an exotic car. The boy looked back admired the car and said to himself “ I am going to drive a better car in this town”. That was decades ago, today that boy now a man is perhaps the richest person in that town of course with the best cars in that town but he took some steps. We’ll return to in the article. Brethren, let’s go to the spiritual. The word of the Lord tells us in Proverbs 18 vs. 21 ( NIV) “ the tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it eat its fruit”. The son of a farmer used his tongue positively and he is eating the fruits of the words that he spoke to himself today. As Christians however, we need not use the tongue casually as the farmer’s son did. We need to use the tongue in line with the word of God. How then do we use the appropriate word? The answer is found in the word of Prophet Joshua in Joshua 1 vs.8: “ Do not let this Book of the Law depart from your mouth; meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do every written in it. Then you will be prosperous and successful”. The importance of tongue that God has given to all human beings is repeated in Psalm 1 vs. 2: “ But his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on his law he meditates day and night”. Just as you need to study to pass an exam you need to study the Word of God to be able to confess it. Confession in this case is not about the sins you have committed but it’s about saying what God has promised you and your desire to have it. To confess it, you need to memorize that particular verse of the Bible and say it to yourself. In other words, you need to put the words you have memorized into action by saying it to yourself and as you do so, if no human being sees you, the invisible God is watching and listening to you. How do I know? I knew a woman that was barren for over 20 years. She learnt the word by going to church regularly and reading the Holy Bible on her own. It was during one of those church services that she picked up two verses. The first, is Deuteronomy 7 vs. 14: “ You will be blessed more than any other people, none of your men or women will be childless, nor any of your livestock without young”. The second is Exodus 23 vs.26: “ and none shall miscarry or be barren in your land. I will give you a full life span”. These two passages are quite relevant for anyone waiting on the Lord for children. Before this woman who had been waiting on the LORD for decades conceived, she made up her mind that she wanted a set of twins. She found the word in the story of Rebecca recorded in Genesis 25 vs. 23 &24: “ The LORD said to her, Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you will be separated, one will be stronger than the other and the older will serve the younger” Verse 24: “When the time came for her to give birth, there were twin boys in her womb”. The key word her is in verse 24. This woman began to say to herself, while bathing, “ I am a mother of twins”. Touching her stomach, she would say “ This my body would produce a set of twins”. She did this regularly while bathing. No one heard her but God, her Creator heard her. What she did was using her tongue to claim her right in the Lord. That was action taken. The son of the farmer also took action by studying. He continued to study even after he had his first degree and had begun working. With determination despite his work schedule, he got two other degrees. God favoured him and he got jobs as chief executive in a lucrative industry. On her part, the woman waiting on the Lord for a set of twins first had a son and about 18 months, later because she didn’t stop confessing the birth of twins, she gave birth to set of twins; two girls. Brethren, the two testimonies shared are about one that wanted divine prosperity and the childless woman that became fruitful. Both used the tongue to pronounce the Word and the result was testimony. Several examples of the use of the tongue are found in the Bible. God used the Word and the Word produced results. Genesis 1 vs.2&3 are my witness. It states, “ Now the earth was formless and empty, darkness was over the surface of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters. And God said “ Let there be light; and there was light”. The idea of how to end darkness was not put into use until God made a pronouncement. The LORD said, it and it manifested. The pronouncement is an action taken by God. That pronouncement is the reason we have day and night till today. Brethren, what are you using your tongue for? If you say, “ nothing can happen to me this year”, nothing is what you will get. If you say however, that “ before this month ends, I will testify to the goodness of God, that is what you will get. What you say is what you get but you must take action. Those that find the word and refuse to confess it and take action will get nothing. Whereas, those that find the word, take action and confess the word always enter into a season of testimonies. Beloved, may your testimony manifest before year 2026 comes to an end. Dear Believer, you still have time to find the word and speak it into that situation that you want changed for the better. Perhaps, you have remained single for years and people have concluded that you would die single. This is the time to speak the Word. Use the Word to bring about your desired miracle. As you confess the word daily, be confident, that Jesus, our advocate hears you and since the LORD hears you, at his own time, the challenge would end. Victory is ours in Jesus name. The post Receive what you confess, by Funmi Komolafe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Luv FM’s Clinton Yeboah wins Best Radio Feature at 30th GJA Media Awards
items.description: Luv FM journalist Clinton Yeboah has won the Best Radio Feature award at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards held in Accra on November 7, 2026. The award recognises his work in radio feature production and adds to a series of honours he has received for his journalism. Earlier in 2026, Mr Yeboah won two first-place awards in the Health and Business/Economy Journalism categories at the GJA Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards. The latest recognition extends his award record across different areas of journalism. Mr Yeboah works with Luv FM, a subsidiary of the Multimedia Group Limited. The 30th GJA Media Awards were held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Advancing Media Freedom and Combating Hate Speech in the Digital Age.” The ceremony brought together journalists, media organisations and other stakeholders to recognise contributions to journalism in Ghana.

items.title: Israël: dans le désert du Néguev, les Bédouins se sont mobilisés aux législatives face aux démolitions
items.description: Dimanche 8 novembre, le président israélien Isaac Herzog confiera à Gadi Eisenkot la charge de former un gouvernement. Le rival de Benyamin Netanyahu est soutenu par six partis, dont des partis arabes. Les électeurs arabes israéliens se sont particulièrement mobilisés lors de ces législatives. Habituellement, ils ne sont pas si nombreux à aller voter. Cette fois, face à la peur inspirée par le ministre d'extrême droite Itamar Ben Gvir et face à la multiplication des démolitions de villages jugés illégaux par Israël, ils sont allés aux urnes.

items.title: GJA calls for better pay and conditions to protect media independence
items.description: The Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) has called for improved remuneration and working conditions for journalists, warning that poor welfare threatens media independence and professional integrity. President of the Association, Albert Dwumfour, said the economic conditions under which many journalists work continue to undermine the dignity and independence of the profession. Speaking at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra, he identified poor remuneration, insecure employment, inadequate conditions of service, irregular salary payments and limited opportunities for professional development as persistent challenges facing media practitioners. “Poor remuneration, insecure employment, inadequate conditions of service, irregular salaries, and limited opportunities for professional development continue to undermine the dignity and independence of journalists,” he said. Mr Dwumfour argued that journalists who struggle to meet their basic needs could become more vulnerable to undue influence and professional compromise. “Improving journalist welfare is therefore not simply a labour issue. It is an investment in media independence, professional integrity and the quality of our democracy,” he said. He stressed that the media industry must address the economic realities of journalists if it expects them to uphold professional standards and hold public institutions accountable. The GJA President said the Association could not demand courageous, independent and ethical journalism while overlooking the conditions under which media practitioners operate. “Those who dedicate their lives to informing society, holding power accountable, and defending the public interest deserve decent working conditions and a dignified standard of living,” he stated. The Association has intensified engagement with Parliament on the need for legislative intervention to improve journalists’ conditions of service. It is also seeking to work with Parliament, media owners and labour stakeholders to develop a framework for addressing concerns about remuneration, job security and the general welfare of media practitioners.

items.title: Ini Dima Okojie reflects on changes motherhood brings
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Ini Dima Okojie has reflected on the changes motherhood has brought into her life as she celebrates her son’s six-month milestone. The Blood Sisters actress shared photographs of her son on social media, expressing amazement at how quickly time had passed since she first met him. “Pinch me. I’m a mother to a six-month-old! How is this even possible? It feels like just yesterday I was meeting you for the very first time,” she wrote. Describing the past six months as surreal, Okojie said watching her son grow and change daily had been a source of joy for the family. She described him as their “little bundle of joy” and prayed for God’s continued protection over him. Beyond the celebration, the actress has also spoken about adjusting to the realities of motherhood. In an earlier message to new mothers, Okojie acknowledged that the experience had brought significant changes to her life and that she was still finding her way through them. She encouraged women to be patient with themselves, noting that they might not look or feel the same as they did before childbirth. According to her, new mothers should give themselves grace and time to adjust, while recognising the remarkable changes their bodies have undergone. Okojie announced the arrival of her baby boy on June 24, 2026, while celebrating her birthday. Following the birth, she shared a video of her labour room experience on Instagram, paying tribute to mothers and describing women as superheroes. On Mother’s Day, the actress also celebrated her new role, expressing disbelief that she could now celebrate the occasion as a mother herself. Her latest milestone offers another glimpse into her experience of motherhood, a journey she has shared with fans through personal reflections on childbirth and adjusting to life with a newborn. The post Ini Dima Okojie reflects on changes motherhood brings appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: I’m in love and in money’, Sotayo Gaga says
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Sotayo Gaga has said she enjoys both love and financial stability, declaring that she is “in love and in money”. The actress made this known during an appearance on Isbae U’s podcast, Curiosity Made Me Ask, where she responded to a series of questions from the comedian. Asked whether she was in love or in money, Gaga replied, “The two, both of them. I am in love and I am in money.” She also spoke about her husband, offering a brief but emphatic response when asked about him. “My husband is not hungry. My husband is very okay,” she said. In another exchange, the actress offered an interesting response when the conversation turned to other women potentially laying claim to her husband. “To me, he is my husband. He might be ‘our’ husband. One can only speak for oneself. To me, he might be my husband, but he might be our husband,” she said. Speaking about her acting career, Gaga explained that although she remains passionate about filmmaking, she balances acting with other commitments. “I love to do movies, so when I have time to act, I act. When I don’t have time, I do some other things,” she said. During the conversation, the actress also revealed that the late actor Kamal Adebayo, popularly known as Sir K, once approached her to help connect his son, Isbae U, with Nigerian rapper Olamide, popularly known as Baddo, to kick-start a music career. items.title: L'exposition nationale itinérante "60 ans de peinture au Maroc" fait escale à Marrakech
items.description: Le vernissage de l’exposition nationale itinérante « 60 ans de peinture au Maroc » a eu lieu, vendredi à la Galerie des Arts du Centre culturel Daoudiate, à Marrakech, en présence d’une pléiade d’artistes, de personnalités du monde de la culture et de passionnés d’arts plastiques. Placée sous le haut patronage du Roi Mohammed VI, cette manifestation, organisée par le Syndicat Marocain des Artistes Plasticiens Professionnels (SMAPP), vise à retracer six décennies de création plastique au Maroc, à mettre en valeur la diversité des courants et des sensibilités artistiques et à contribuer à la préservation de la mémoire culturelle nationale. S’inscrivant dans le cadre de la célébration de la Glorieuse Marche Verte et de la Fête de l’Unité, cette exposition réunit des œuvres d’artistes pionniers et contemporains, offrant au public une vision panoramique de l’évolution des arts plastiques au Maroc, depuis les premières générations et les grandes figures jusqu’aux créateurs actuels. Prévu jusqu’au 30 novembre courant, cet événement permet ainsi aux visiteurs de découvrir la diversité des styles, des techniques, des thématiques et des approches qui ont marqué six décennies de création plastique nationale. A noter que l’étape de Marrakech a également été marquée par l’organisation d’une autre exposition à la Khalid Fine Art Gallery, au cours de laquelle un hommage sera rendu à l’artiste peintre Omar Bouragba pour l’ensemble de son parcours artistique. Un colloque consacré aux enjeux futurs et aux perspectives des arts plastiques a également été organisé jeudi, et a permis de mettre en regard les expériences des pionniers et des générations précédentes avec les nouvelles pratiques portées notamment par les jeunes artistes. Marrakech constitue la troisième étape de cette exposition nationale itinérante, après Rabat et Casablanca. items.title: UPLG : Minkailou Barry élu président de l’Union de la Presse Libre de Guinée
items.description: Ce samedi 7 novembre 2026 à Conakry, Minkailou Barry est élu président de l'Union de la Presse Libre de Guinée (UPLG). Il a remporté l'élection présidentielle de l'association, organisée lors de son congrès à la Maison de la Presse de Guinée. Directeur de publication du site leverificateur.net, M. Barry occupait jusque-là le poste de secrétaire général de l'organisation. Il affrontait Mohamed Cissé, directeur de publication du média en ligne avenirguinee.org. Le vote s'est soldé par 44 voix pour M. Barry et 14 pour son adversaire. Un bulletin a été déclaré nul. L'huissier de justice, Me Amadou Soumah, a proclamé les résultats devant l'assemblée. La salle était pleine. Journalistes, directeurs de publication et autres acteurs des médias avaient fait le déplacement. Le nouveau président remplace Grégoire Ankou, qui quitte la tête de l'UPLG. Les congressistes ont salué son bilan. Sous sa direction, l'organisation est passée d'une dizaine de membres en 2019 à près d'une centaine aujourd'hui. Après la proclamation, Minkailou Barry a remercié l'ensemble des membres. Il a salué les membres de l'intérieur du pays, notamment ceux de Kankan, ainsi que ceux installés à l'étranger pour leur mobilisation malgré la distance géopolitique. Il a rendu hommage aux pionniers de l'UPLG, dont l'honorable Bahfisher et Ibrahima Koné. Il a également salué le travail de Grégoire Ankou et l'attitude démocratique de son challenger Mohamed Cissé. Le président élu a insisté sur la cohésion de l'organisation. « Il n'y a pas d'UPLG du candidat A, ni d'UPLG du candidat B. L'UPLG est une et indivisible », a-t-il déclaré. Le bureau exécutif compte 11 membres. Il a fixé trois axes de travail, face aux enjeux du numérique, de l'intelligence artificielle et de l'équilibre financier des rédactions. Le premier axe concerne la formation continue et la déontologie. L'objectif est de renforcer les compétences des journalistes et de garantir une information rigoureuse. Le deuxième porte sur la viabilité économique. L'UPLG veut conclure des partenariats pour structurer les rédactions et améliorer les conditions de travail dans les entreprises de presse membres. Le troisième vise la solidarité et la protection des membres. L'organisation entend soutenir juridiquement et moralement les directeurs de publication et les journalistes, à Conakry, à l'intérieur du pays et à l'étranger. Minkailou Barry a conclu son intervention sous les applaudissements. « Le temps des discours est fini, l'heure est à l'action », a-t-il affirmé. items.title: Maroc : 60 % des citoyens estiment que la corruption est répandue dans les institutions
items.description: Le neuvième cycle du Baromètre arabe consacré au Maroc, portant sur l’année 2025, met en évidence les préoccupations économiques et sociales des citoyens. Près de six Marocains sur dix jugent la situation économique mauvaise, tandis que 60 % estiment que la corruption est présente à un degré important ou moyen dans les institutions publiques. L’enquête relève toutefois une progression de la confiance envers le Parlement et le gouvernement, ainsi qu’une amélioration de l’évaluation de l’action gouvernementale. Le coût de la vie, le chômage, la pauvreté et l’insécurité alimentaire figurent parmi les principales préoccupations des Marocains. C’est ce qui ressort des résultats du neuvième cycle du Baromètre arabe consacré au Maroc et couvrant l’année 2025. L’étude met également en évidence une insatisfaction persistante à l’égard de la situation économique, ainsi que des inquiétudes concernant la qualité des services publics et la propagation de la corruption. Sur le plan économique, seuls 7 % des répondants considèrent que la situation est très bonne et 34 % la jugent bonne. À l’inverse, 57 % estiment qu’elle est mauvaise ou très mauvaise. Les perspectives à moyen terme restent partagées : un tiers des personnes interrogées ne s’attend à aucun changement au cours des trois prochaines années, tandis que 27 % anticipent une dégradation. Environ 37 % se montrent, à l’inverse, optimistes et prévoient une amélioration importante ou modérée. L’insécurité alimentaire, une préoccupation concrète Les difficultés économiques se traduisent également dans les conditions de vie quotidiennes. Selon l’enquête, 56 % des Marocains déclarent que les aliments achetés au cours des trente jours précédant le sondage ont parfois ou souvent été consommés avant qu’ils disposent de l’argent nécessaire pour en acheter davantage. Les résultats font aussi état de privations alimentaires au cours de l’année précédente. Ainsi, 34 % des répondants indiquent avoir dû se limiter à quelques types d’aliments faute de ressources suffisantes. Quelque 29 % déclarent avoir sauté un repas, tandis que 32 % affirment que la nourriture est effectivement venue à manquer dans leur foyer. Ces difficultés touchent particulièrement les personnes qui ne disposent pas de revenus suffisants pour couvrir leurs besoins essentiels. Les jeunes apparaissent également davantage exposés à l’inquiétude de ne pas avoir suffisamment de nourriture que les catégories plus âgées. Interrogés sur les problèmes économiques les plus préoccupants pour le Maroc, les citoyens placent l’inflation en tête, suivie de la pauvreté et du manque de logements abordables. Les bas salaires, l’insuffisance des opportunités d’emploi, l’accès au crédit et les inégalités entre riches et pauvres figurent également parmi les difficultés citées. La santé et le développement économique en tête des priorités Les attentes exprimées à l’égard de l’action publique reflètent ces préoccupations. La santé et le développement économique arrivent en tête des priorités budgétaires, chacun étant cité par 19 % des répondants. Le soutien public recueille 18 % des préférences, devant les routes et les transports, puis l’éducation. L’appréciation des services publics révèle, pour sa part, des niveaux de satisfaction contrastés. La fourniture d’électricité recueille 62 % d’avis favorables et celle de l’eau 57 %. En revanche, la satisfaction concernant le système de santé s’établit à 45 %, contre 48 % pour le système éducatif. Ces deux secteurs restent donc en dessous du seuil de 50 %. L’enquête relève par ailleurs une préférence de 45 % des Marocains pour un emploi dans le secteur public plutôt que dans le privé, principalement en raison de la stabilité professionnelle et des rémunérations jugées meilleures. Dans le même temps, 39 % des personnes interrogées estiment que l’accès à un emploi nécessite de disposer de relations ou de bénéficier de pratiques de favoritisme. La corruption reste une source d’inquiétude La perception de la corruption constitue un autre enseignement important du Baromètre arabe. Selon les résultats, 60 % des répondants considèrent que la corruption est répandue à un degré important ou moyen dans les institutions de l’État. En parallèle, près de la moitié des personnes interrogées, soit 47 %, estiment que le gouvernement mène des actions pour lutter contre ce phénomène. Ces chiffres traduisent ainsi une perception qui associe la persistance de la corruption à une reconnaissance, par une partie de la population, des efforts déployés pour la combattre. Une confiance institutionnelle en progression Malgré les réserves exprimées sur la situation économique et la corruption, l’enquête fait état d’une progression de la confiance envers plusieurs institutions politiques. Celle accordée au Parlement est passée de 38 % à 51 %, tandis que celle envers le gouvernement a progressé de 33 % à 52 %. Le taux de confiance envers l’ancien chef du gouvernement est également passé de 30 % à 45 %, selon les données du sondage. Par ailleurs, près d’un Marocain sur deux se déclare satisfait ou très satisfait de la performance globale du gouvernement. Cette proportion atteint 50 %, contre 29 % lors de la précédente édition, soit une progression de 21 points de pourcentage. La hiérarchie des institutions bénéficiant de la confiance des citoyens place toujours l’armée en première position, suivie de la police, de la justice et de la société civile. Le Parlement et le gouvernement viennent ensuite, devant le chef du gouvernement. Enfin, le Baromètre arabe relève un intérêt relativement élevé pour la politique au Maroc. Quelque 42 % des personnes interrogées déclarent s’y intéresser ou s’y intéresser fortement. Il s’agit, selon l’enquête, de la proportion la plus élevée parmi les pays couverts par cette édition du Baromètre. Cet intérêt concerne aussi bien les hommes que les femmes et se retrouve dans les différentes catégories d’âge, sans se traduire nécessairement par une participation équivalente aux organisations et associations. items.title: GJA criticises Sam George over comments on media closures and engagement with Mahama
items.description: The Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) has criticised the Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, over comments suggesting that its President, Albert Dwumfour, sought President John Dramani Mahama’s intervention following the minister’s remarks about shutting down politically and religiously affiliated media organisations. Mr Dwumfour described the comments as unfortunate, insisting that the Association has a responsibility to speak out whenever the rights, welfare and livelihoods of journalists are threatened. Speaking at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra, he said the Association’s engagement with the President was neither personal nor partisan but part of its mandate to protect journalists. “On November 2nd, 2026, at a media program in Accra, the Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Honourable Samuel Nartey George, made comments suggesting that the president of the GJA had run to President John Dramani Mahama, our own member, following the minister’s decision to shut down some radio stations,” he said. “We consider those comments unfortunate, particularly coming from a minister whose portfolio places him at the centre of the country’s communications and media ecosystem.” The minister’s November 2 remarks, made at a public forum in Accra, included a statement that he would shut down politically and religiously affiliated media houses if he had the authority to do so. Mr Dwumfour said the Association could not remain silent when decisions affecting media organisations threatened the employment and welfare of journalists. “That responsibility is neither personal nor partisan. It is at the heart of our mandate as a professional body representing journalists in Ghana,” he said. He expressed concern about the potential impact of media closures on workers, particularly given what he described as the already poor and precarious conditions of service in parts of the industry. “I do not expect the GJA to remain silent when members of our association whose conditions of service are already poor and precarious are suddenly thrown out of employment as a consequence of decisions to shut down media organizations. 64 media organizations for that matter,” he stated. The GJA President acknowledged the importance of regulating the broadcasting industry but insisted that enforcement must be transparent, fair and proportionate. He argued that regulatory breaches should not automatically result in workers losing their livelihoods. “The fact that a media organization may have breached a regulatory requirement should not automatically make the livelihood of its workers collateral damage,” he said. “We must be careful not to create a situation in which the exercise of regulatory authority becomes an instrument that leaves journalists and other media practitioners without jobs.” Mr Dwumfour also commended President Mahama for what he described as a timely intervention following the Association’s appeal. He said the President had responded to the GJA’s concerns and issued clemency within two hours. “I must, on this note, once again on behalf of the inky fraternity commend the President, who is a listening leader, for listening to our cry and issuing clemency within two hours. We insist that the President did what is within his remit and good for this profession,” he said. The GJA says it will continue engaging the President, ministers, Parliament, regulators and media owners whenever developments threaten the safety, welfare and professional independence of journalists.

items.title: One dead, five injured in clash at Asaba political rally
items.description: One person has been killed and five others injured in a violent clash during a political rally organised by the Obedient/OK Movement in support of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Asaba, Delta State. The incident occurred at about 12:15 p.m. on Saturday, 7 November 2026, along Nnebisi Road in Asaba. The identities of the victims are yet to be established. According to a statement by the Delta State Police Command, the police had received an intelligence report indicating the likelihood of violence and invited the organisers to a security meeting. “During the engagement, they were briefed on the identified security threats and advised against holding an open road procession. They were further encouraged to conduct their political activities at a designated venue where appropriate security will be provided for them. However, the organisers ignored this important security advice and proceeded with the road procession,” the statement said. Upon receiving a distress call, police operatives mobilised to the scene and took the injured victims to the hospital for medical attention. Security was subsequently reinforced in the affected area to forestall further breakdown of law and order, while investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. Commissioner of Police Samuel E. Erale condemned the violence and reiterated that political parties are free to conduct lawful campaigns and other political activities. “He, however, advises all political parties and their supporters to avoid road processions in the interest of public safety and to liaise with the Police ahead of any political gatherings to facilitate adequate security arrangements,” the statement said. The CP assured residents of Delta State of the Command’s commitment to a thorough and impartial investigation and urge anyone with useful information to contact the Command through the following phone numbers; 09155570008 or 09155570007. items.title: Real Madrid beat Valencia to level Liga leaders Barca
items.description: Kylian Mbappe scored for the seventh match running as Real Madrid pulled provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a 3-0 win at 10-man Valencia on Saturday. Reigning champions Barca visit Atletico Madrid, third, on Sunday, aiming to move back clear of the chasing pack. Jose Mourinho’s Madrid largely dominated at Mestalla stadium as they secured an eighth win in a row across all competitions. Federico Valverde and Arda Guler’s first half goals put Madrid in the driving seat and Mbappe added a third in the second half. Los Blancos were without winger Vinicius Junior, who was serving the final game of a four-match ban. Madrid have thrived in his absence, putting heavy pressure on Barca, whom they beat in the Camp Nou Clasico on October 25. In the ninth minutes the match stopped for players and fans to pay tribute to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who tragically died on Tuesday. Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made a smart save to deny Aaron Mayol, who had picked Aurelien Tchouameni’s pocket in a dangerous area. Valencia’s Guido Rodriguez had a goal disallowed for offside before Mourinho’s side took control. Valverde drilled Madrid ahead from outside the area after Mbappe’s free-kick was blocked by the Valencia wall and fell to the Uruguayan. Guler soon doubled the lead, after Jude Bellingham’s cross was deflected kindly into his path. Guler had a good chance for the third in early in the second half but Valencia goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski grabbed the ball as the midfielder tried to round him. Minutes later Dimitrievski saved well from Mbappe as the French striker ran through and tried to dink the ball over him. Bellingham powered his way through the defence and was also denied by the goalkeeper, as was Mbappe following up with an overhead kick, as Madrid tried to find a third to kill off the game. Eventually Mbappe produced it, bursting onto a dangerous pass by Guler to dart past Dimitrievski and squeeze home his 13th league goal of the campaign. It was the forward’s 17th goal in 16 games across all competitions. Mbappe has netted in his last seven appearances for Madrid. Valencia’s Jose Gaya was dismissed with around 10 minutes remaining for a late sliding foul on Mbappe to further spoil Javier Aguirre’s team’s night. Earlier new Espanyol coach Eder Sarabia’s side were held to a goalless home draw by Deportivo La Coruna. Osasuna snatched a late 1-1 draw against Athletic Bilbao, while Racing Santander came from behind to beat Malaga 2-1.
