items.title: Tomates : Après la suspension des exportations vers l’Afrique, les prix reculent sur les marchés marocains
items.description: Après avoir atteint 17 dirhams le kilogramme dans certains marchés, les prix des tomates ont amorcé une baisse sur les marchés de détail. Samedi, le produit se négociait entre 13 et 15 dirhams le kilogramme, contre 17 dirhams auparavant, selon les constatations de Hespress . Des détaillants interrogés dans plusieurs marchés populaires et de proximité de Rabat ont confirmé cette évolution. Cette baisse intervient alors que les autorités marocaines ont suspendu les exportations de tomates vers les marchés africains. Dans un contexte de tensions ponctuelles sur les prix et l’approvisionnement, le gouvernement affirme poursuivre ses efforts pour stabiliser les marchés nationaux. Une source gouvernementale a indiqué à Hespress que l’exécutif travaillait à assurer une stabilité maximale des prix et un approvisionnement régulier du marché national au cours des prochains jours. Les données officielles arrêtées au 5 novembre 2026 font néanmoins apparaître des évolutions contrastées des prix de certains légumes, fruits et œufs par rapport à l’année précédente. Un retard de maturation dans le Souss-Massa La hausse récente des prix de certains produits, en particulier des tomates, s’explique principalement par des facteurs climatiques conjoncturels, selon la source gouvernementale. Dans la région du Souss-Massa, importante zone de production, la récolte précoce des tomates a accusé un retard relatif en raison de la baisse des températures enregistrée depuis le mois d’octobre. Ce refroidissement a ralenti la maturation des cultures et temporairement réduit les volumes de production acheminés vers le marché national. La source précise toutefois que les prix restent stables sur le marché de gros de référence d’Inezgane, où le kilogramme de tomates s’établit à 6,7 dirhams. Des évolutions contrastées pour les produits alimentaires Au-delà des tomates, les données gouvernementales font état d’une baisse du prix des œufs vendus à l’unité. Celui-ci s’établit désormais à une moyenne nationale de 1,3 dirham, contre un niveau supérieur l’année précédente. Les prix des fruits connaissent, dans leur ensemble, une relative stabilité. Les oranges se distinguent néanmoins par une diminution de 6 % par rapport à la même période de l’année dernière. Les coûts de l’alimentation animale suivent également une tendance à la baisse. L’orge, la paille et le son enregistrent un recul significatif, attribué à l’amélioration de la production céréalière au cours de la campagne agricole 2025-2026. Cette évolution devrait contribuer à réduire les coûts de production de l’élevage. Le gouvernement mise sur le pic de production saisonnière Pour préserver le pouvoir d’achat des ménages et garantir la continuité de l’approvisionnement, les services du ministère de l’agriculture assurent un suivi de la disponibilité de la production nationale, en coordination avec les différents acteurs du secteur. L’objectif est notamment de compenser les retards ponctuels de maturation des cultures provoqués par la baisse des températures et de maintenir un approvisionnement suffisant des marchés. Le ministère de tutelle anticipe un rééquilibrage progressif des prix dans les prochains jours, à mesure que les différentes filières de fruits et légumes entreront dans leur pic de production saisonnière. Cette montée en puissance de l’offre devrait contribuer à réduire la pression sur les consommateurs et à favoriser une stabilisation des marchés. The post Tomates : Après la suspension des exportations vers l’Afrique, les prix reculent sur les marchés marocains appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Burkina Faso : La fabrication et la vente des produits de la gamme « Cyclone » suspendues
items.description: À travers un communiqué rendu public ce 7 novembre 2026, la Faso Food and Drug Administration (Faso FDA) a annoncé la suspension de la fabrication et de la commercialisation des produits de la gamme « Cyclone » sur le territoire burkinabè. Cette décision fait suite à des analyses de laboratoire ayant révélé la présence de sildénafil dans des échantillons de ces produits. Selon la Faso FDA, les analyses effectuées sur des échantillons de jus commercialisés sous la dénomination « Cyclone » par la société YELEMANY BAA SARL, basée à Bobo-Dioulasso, ont mis en évidence la présence de sildénafil. Le sildénafil est une substance médicamenteuse utilisée dans le traitement des troubles de l’érection. Son utilisation nécessite un encadrement médical en raison des risques qu’elle présente, notamment chez les personnes souffrant de maladies cardiovasculaires ou d’hypertension, les personnes âgées ainsi que celles prenant des dérivés nitrés. La présence de cette substance n’étant pas mentionnée sur l’étiquetage des produits concernés, présentés comme des boissons ou des compléments alimentaires « 100 % naturels », la Faso FDA appelle la population à la vigilance. Les produits concernés par cette mesure sont : « Cyclone Classique », « Cyclone Retard », « Cyclone Sirop » et « Cyclone Poudre », quels que soient leur numéro de lot et leur lieu d’achat. items.title: Gas transportation network not responsible for power generation drop – NNPC
items.description: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) has said its gas transportation network remains available to supply gas to power generating stations nationwide, insisting that transportation constraints are not responsible for the current decline in electricity generation. The national oil company said operational records of its subsidiary, NNPC Gas Infrastructure Company Limited (NGIC), showed no transportation-related constraints within its network that could explain the drop in power generation. NNPC disclosed this in a statement issued by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, in Abuja on Friday. The clarification followed a November 5 statement by the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), which attributed the decline in electricity generation partly to limited gas availability and reduced water inflows into hydroelectric power stations. However, NNPC said its clarification was specifically about the operational status of its gas transportation infrastructure, noting that gas production, commercial supply arrangements and actual deliveries to individual power plants were separate issues requiring independent assessment. The company said gas production had grown by about 10 per cent year-to-date in 2026, attributing the increase to the Federal Government’s gas development and monetisation agenda. “Gas supply availability is therefore not a challenge as NNPC remains committed to supporting efforts to improve electricity generation through safe, reliable and efficient gas supply and transportation,” the statement said. NNPC further explained that determining the causes of the generation shortfall required an assessment of other components of the gas-to-power value chain. These, it said, included the availability and operational readiness of generating units, plant maintenance schedules and actual gas offtake by power stations. The company stressed that the factors must be examined alongside gas supply data to establish the specific causes of the decline in electricity generation. It also called for a coordinated review of operational data by gas suppliers, transporters, power generators and NISO to identify constraints and guide appropriate interventions. NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to developing dependable energy infrastructure and collaborating with stakeholders to translate the country’s gas resources into more reliable electricity supply for Nigerians. The post Gas transportation network not responsible for power generation drop – NNPC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: IOTA Leadership Dealership 2026 challenges young people to become solution-driven leaders
items.description: Africa’s growing youth population presents a major opportunity for the continent, but persistent unemployment, weak institutional accountability and rapid technological change are raising questions about whether young people are adequately prepared to shape its future. With millions entering the labour market, speakers at the second Leadership Dealership Conference organised by the IOTA Ministry Groupe have urged young Africans to develop the values, skills and sense of responsibility needed to lead in an increasingly complex world. The conference brought together speakers from business, technology and faith to examine the character, competence and discipline required for impactful leadership. For the convenor and President of the IOTA Ministry Group, Apostle Joseph Kwadwo Yeboah, effective leadership begins not with the desire to be in charge but with the willingness to learn from others. “Nobody was born a leader. Leadership is the consequence of right following,” he said. Speaking on the theme, The Structure and Function of Impactful Leadership , Apostle Yeboah argued that people must first learn from those who have gone ahead of them before they can effectively lead others. Drawing on Jesus Christ’s calling of His first disciples in Matthew 4:18–20, he said leadership development requires intentional relationships, guidance and personal commitment. He identified intention, invention and intervention as three essential elements of impactful leadership. Intention, he explained, provides direction and vision; invention drives creativity and problem-solving; while intervention requires leaders to take responsibility and act when circumstances demand it. He also stressed the importance of trust and relationships, arguing that professional competence, communication skills and charisma must be supported by sound moral values. Apostle Yeboah further challenged participants to translate their faith into practical responsibility, saying spirituality should be reflected in their everyday conduct. “If there is no deadline, it is not a discipline yet,” he said, emphasising that good intentions must be matched by accountability and action. Young people urged to take initiative Chief Executive Officer of Henos Energy, Henry Osei, urged young people to stop waiting for leadership opportunities and instead demonstrate their ability to solve problems. He said everyone had the potential to lead, but developing that potential required the right environment, guidance and relationships. “Find a mentor and go where you want to be,” he advised, encouraging participants to seek guidance from people who had already achieved the goals they hoped to accomplish. Mr Osei recounted forming a small group of promising young men with whom he held brainstorming sessions twice a week. Within five years, he said, members of the group had progressed into leadership positions. He challenged participants to move beyond simply attending work or church without making meaningful contributions. For him, leadership is demonstrated through ownership, initiative and the ability to provide solutions rather than merely identify problems. “Leadership means owning the result,” he said. AI and automation reshape leadership demands While mentorship and personal discipline remain important, futurist Kwame AA Opoku said young Africans must also prepare for a future in which technology is changing the nature of work and professional competence. The founder of the African AI Governance Index, who spoke on Leadership in 2035 , said decisions being made today would influence how individuals, institutions and countries navigate the next five to ten years. He pointed to advances in artificial intelligence, robotics and automation, warning that no profession should assume it is immune to technological disruption. Citing developments in robotic kitchens, self-driving vehicles, flying taxis and police robots, he illustrated how technology is increasingly taking over tasks traditionally performed by humans. Mr Opoku also raised ethical concerns about gene editing, artificial wombs and deepfakes, warning that technological advances could create challenges for human identity, trust and the ability to distinguish fact from fabrication. He expressed concern about the growing use of artificial intelligence for spiritual guidance, saying it raised questions about human judgement, parenting and wisdom. “This is not an IT problem,” he stressed. He said Africa faced particular risks if its growing youth population was not matched by sufficient employment opportunities, warning that the resulting pressures could deepen social tensions and instability. Drawing lessons from unrest in Tunisia, Sudan, Sri Lanka, Kenya and Serbia, he cautioned against development strategies that focused only on immediate needs without accounting for long-term realities. “If you build for the short term, you build for a world that is already dead,” he said. Africa must leverage its strengths Despite the challenges, Mr Opoku said Africa had strengths it could use to navigate the changing technological landscape. He identified reputation-based markets, a culture of presence, oral intellect and relationships as forms of capital that could become increasingly valuable in a world saturated with artificial content and manufactured identities. He urged young people to invest in their intellectual development, understand how systems work and recognise their responsibility in shaping the quality of leadership across the continent. “We don’t have a leadership problem. We have a citizens problem,” he said. The discussions at the conference highlighted the need for young Africans to look beyond the pursuit of positions and focus on developing the capacity to make meaningful contributions to their communities. The speakers’ messages placed emphasis on mentorship, discipline, problem-solving, ethical conduct and an understanding of emerging technologies as important elements of leadership preparation.

items.title: Olawepo-Hashim visits Sowore, condemns political violence
items.description: Former presidential candidate, Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has condemned political violence in Nigeria, warning that attacks on political opponents could worsen the country’s already precarious security situation. Olawepo-Hashim also called on President Bola Tinubu to caution members of his team against actions and statements capable of provoking political conflict. He made the remarks in a statement posted on his X platform on Saturday after visiting activist and publisher, Omoyele Sowore, following the reported attack on him in Ekiti State. Olawepo-Hashim said his visit was motivated by their longstanding relationship, which dates back to their participation in the struggle against military dictatorship and the campaign for democracy. He warned that Nigeria, already grappling with terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other security challenges, could not afford another crisis arising from political violence. “Nigeria cannot afford to add political violence to the general insecurity in the land. “Nigeria is already battling terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and widespread insecurity. We cannot afford to add political violence to this burden,” he said. The former presidential candidate welcomed a statement by a United Nations representative expressing concern over the incident and urged other international partners to condemn political violence. He also urged political leaders to exercise restraint, warning that those who provoke violence might not be the ones to suffer its consequences. “President Bola Tinubu must call his team to order. Political leaders must exercise restraint and stop actions or rhetoric capable of provoking conflict. Those who recklessly provoke violence may not be the ones who bear its consequences,” he said. Recalling their history, Olawepo-Hashim said he and Sowore had been comrades since 1989/1990, when they worked together against military rule. He said he was particularly moved by Sowore’s recollection of how he introduced him to political activism at the University of Lagos. According to him, Sowore reaffirmed during the visit that he remained undeterred by the reported attack and was determined to continue campaigning for genuine democracy. Olawepo-Hashim stressed that political disagreements should not be used as justification for violence, urging Nigerians to uphold democratic values and reject actions capable of worsening insecurity and instability in the country. The post Olawepo-Hashim visits Sowore, condemns political violence appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Medical Superintendents call for stronger emergency care to tackle no-bed syndrome
items.description: The Medical Superintendents Group is calling for an expansion of emergency and critical care facilities, alongside improvements in hospital referral systems, to address Ghana’s persistent no-bed syndrome. The group says tackling the problem will require political commitment, sustainable financing and stronger collaboration among healthcare institutions. Speaking at the 68th Annual General Conference of the Ghana Medical Association (GMA), a representative of the group said hospital managers experienced the challenges associated with the no-bed syndrome firsthand. “Where we sit, we experience, firsthand, all the challenges associated with the no-bed syndrome,” the representative said. The group is advocating a stronger National Ambulance Service, improved pre-hospital emergency care and real-time bed management systems to help hospitals respond more effectively to emergencies. It is also calling for a better distribution of skilled emergency healthcare personnel and effective public-private partnerships to expand access to emergency services. The representative stressed that individual hospitals and medical practitioners could not resolve the problem without broader institutional and government support. “The no-bed syndrome, as we know, cannot be addressed by individual hospitals, nor by doctors alone. It requires a strong political commitment,” the representative said. The group believes the proposed measures would improve emergency response and reduce deaths associated with delays in accessing medical treatment. It says its ultimate goal is to ensure that no Ghanaian dies because of the lack of a hospital bed, an ambulance or timely emergency care.

items.title: Journalism educators from 10 countries to meet in Accra for disinformation conference
items.description: Journalism educators and media professionals from 10 countries across the Sahel and West Africa will meet in Accra from November 11 to 13 for a conference focused on tackling disinformation and strengthening information integrity. The inaugural STREAC Autumn School will examine media and information literacy, information manipulation and the growing impact of artificial intelligence on journalism and journalism education. The three-day event will be held at the La Palm Royal Beach Hotel and feature workshops, research presentations and discussions among participants. It is being organised by the Department of Journalism and Media Studies at the University of Education, Winneba (UEW), in partnership with the Erich-Brost Institute for International Journalism at the Technical University of Dortmund in Germany. Germany’s Ambassador to Ghana, Frederik Landshöft, is expected to attend the opening ceremony. He will be joined by Professor Susanne Fengler, Director of the Erich-Brost Institute, and UEW Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Professor Esther Yeboah Danso Wiredu. The conference forms part of the STREAC Disinfo project, funded by the German Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The project seeks to equip journalism educators with the skills and knowledge to address disinformation and information manipulation. It also aims to improve media and information literacy and strengthen journalists’ ability to respond to the spread of false and misleading information.

items.title: Émigration irrégulière : 17 présumés passeurs arrêtés et 114 migrants secourus
items.description: La Division nationale de lutte contre le trafic de migrants et pratiques assimilées (DNLT) a démantelé plusieurs réseaux présumés de trafic de migrants à travers trois opérations menées par son antenne régionale de Ziguinchor. Selon un communiqué de la DNLT, ces interventions ont permis l’interpellation de 17 individus et la prise en charge de 114 candidats à l’émigration irrégulière. Des pirogues, du carburant et des vivres ont également été saisis. La première opération a permis de déjouer un projet de départ vers l’Espagne depuis la Gambie, prévu le 25 octobre 2026. Six individus ont été arrêtés pour association de malfaiteurs et trafic de migrants. Selon les éléments de l’enquête, le réseau préparait le voyage d’environ 175 candidats, auxquels étaient réclamées des sommes comprises entre 400 000 et 500 000 FCFA. Les enquêteurs ont également saisi une pirogue qui aurait été volée au quai de Boudody. La deuxième intervention s’est déroulée le 4 novembre 2026 à Thiobon, en collaboration avec le Commissariat de Bignona. Elle a conduit à l’arrestation de six suspects et à la découverte de 114 candidats à l’émigration irrégulière, de différentes nationalités, dissimulés dans une forêt. Les migrants disposaient de vivres et de carburant en prévision de leur départ. Des opérations entre Kafountine et Joal-Fadiouth La troisième opération, menée à la fin du mois d’octobre à Kafountine et Joal-Fadiouth, a abouti à l’arrestation de cinq autres individus. Parmi eux figurent trois capitaines de pirogue et deux organisateurs présumés. Ils seraient liés à un projet de voyage impliquant environ 200 candidats à l’émigration. Une pirogue a également été saisie. Au total, ces trois opérations portent le bilan à 17 personnes interpellées et 114 candidats secourus ou pris en charge. Le matériel logistique utilisé pour préparer les traversées, notamment des pirogues, du carburant et des vivres, a été saisi. Les investigations se poursuivent à la DNLT afin d'identifier les autres membres de ces réseaux et de remonter l'ensemble de leurs ramifications. C.G.D

items.title: Israeli president picks Netanyahu's rival Gadi Eisenkot to try to form government
items.description: Israel’s president on Saturday chose Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s strongest rival, to try to form a new government following a deadlocked election that left neither man with a clear path to power. Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving leader, is fighting to stay in office after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an Oct 27 election but still emerged as the largest bloc in parliament. Eisenkot, a former military chief, has declined to join forces with Arab parties, with whose support he would have a majority of seats in parliament. But Arab leaders, incensed by what they view as the racist policies of Netanyahu and his far-right allies, still nominated Eisenkot to try to form a government first giving him the most endorsements. “President Herzog has invited Gadi Eisenkot to the President’s Residence, where he will be tasked with forming the government tomorrow,” said the spokesperson of President Isaac Herzog, whose largely ceremonial role involves nominating a candidate to form a coalition after elections. As part of this process, the president met Eisenkot and Netanyahu, among others, a statement by Herzog’s office said. At the end of the consultations, factions comprising 67 Knesset members recommended to the president that Yashar party’s Eisenkot be tasked with forming the government, while factions comprising 46 Knesset members recommended Likud’s Netanyahu, the statement noted. Meanwhile, seven Knesset members chose not to recommend anyone. “Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy,” Eisenkot wrote on X in his first reaction to the announcement of his designation. Eisenkot faces long-shot bid to form govt Weeks of protracted negotiations are expected to follow Eisenkot’s nomination. He has 28 days to try to forge a government, with a possible 14-day extension. His potential pathways to power include trying to form a minority government with Arab support from the outside; forming a coalition with ultra-Orthodox parties that he and his allies have shunned in the past; or forging a unity government with Netanyahu. Analysts say that all three options are unlikely to take shape. If Eisenkot fails, another candidate can try to form a government and if that candidate fails, parliament can nominate another. There is a deadline for the process of around 100 days. If no one succeeds, another election is held. Likud won the most seats of any single party with 27 in the 120-seat Knesset, but Netanyahu’s wider religious-nationalist coalition garnered only 53 in total, short of a 61-seat majority. Eisenkot’s Yashar party emerged as the second-largest party with 21 seats, while his coalition, spanning four centre-left to right-wing Jewish-led parties, won just 48 seats. Two parties representing Israel’s Arab minority won an unprecedented 19 seats. The result underscored the rightward shift among Israeli Jews during Netanyahu’s years as the country’s dominant political figure. The centre-left that dominated Israel for the first half of its history has been reduced to a small fringe. Nearly all Jewish parties now share Netanyahu’s rejection of an eventual independent Palestinian state, the basis of internationally endorsed peace efforts since the 1990s. Eisenkot and Netanyahu have both ​said they would not form a government with parties primarily representing Israeli citizens of Palestinian descent, who comprise around a fifth of the population. A son of Moroccan immigrants, Eisenkot, 66, would be the country’s first prime minister from Israel’s Mizrahi community, Jews who trace their roots to the Middle East and North Africa. Eisenkot only entered politics in 2022. He briefly served in Netanyahu’s wartime cabinet following Hamas’s Oct 7, 2023, attack on Israel before returning to the opposition. Eisenkot’s son and two nephews were killed fighting in Gaza. How different are Eisenkot’s views from Netanyahu? Eisenkot offers a break with Netanyahu’s leadership and far-right allies, but not with the hawkish security views that have hardened since Oct 7, 2023: he opposes Palestinian statehood and says Hamas’s military wing must be destroyed or dismantled. Beyond that, Eisenkot has said Israel’s next government must prevent Iran from acquiring a military nuclear capability, either by force or through an “arrangement” such as a US-backed diplomatic solution. He has emphasised his security credentials on the campaign trail, citing his “ Dahiya doctrine ” of responding to attacks with disproportionate force, which he deployed as a commander during Israel’s 2006 war with Hezbollah in Lebanon. Eisenkot shares many of Netanyahu’s views on security and has backed the Gaza offensive that has reduced the territory to rubble . Israel’s relentless campaign in response to the Hamas attacks killed over 74,000 Palestinians and has left it increasingly isolated on the world stage, with Amnesty International , Human Rights Watch and experts declaring its actions in Gaza as a “genocide”, which Tel Aviv rejects. Both Eisenkot and Netanyahu say Israeli troops will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas ​is disarmed, and that Israel is prepared to ​restart fighting to achieve this. Eisenkot says the ⁠continued rule of Hamas in Gaza is a profound failure, and that within 18 months of taking office he would ensure that the Hamas administration had been replaced, either through a US-brokered plan or through military force. From the opposition, Eisenkot publicly rebuked Netanyahu over his leadership, including his management of the military campaign in Gaza, and has sworn that he would not serve in government with him. Although Eisenkot has criticised settler violence against Palestinians in occupied West Bank, which has surged since 2023, he favours settlement in principle and says it should comply with Israeli law. He opposes settlements built without authorisation, aims to dismantle outposts in areas where ​they are forbidden and has pledged to rein in violent settlers. Hundreds of thousands of Israelis live in the West Bank, settling in territory Israel occupied in a 1967 war, a practice nearly all countries consider illegal under international law. Netanyahu and ​Eisenkot both say Israel must retain ultimate security control over all territory between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea. There are, however, differences in their emphasis. Eisenkot’s position on limiting settlements ​in the West Bank would reserve territory where Palestinians now exercise civil self-rule. Netanyahu’s coalition includes parties that openly call for Israel to fully annex occupied Palestinian land.

items.title: Assemblée nationale : la Commission des Finances rejette les projets de budget
items.description: La Commission des Finances et du Contrôle budgétaire de l’Assemblée nationale a rejeté, samedi 7 novembre 2026, l’ensemble des projets de budget soumis à son examen. Les prévisions de recettes et de dette publique, ainsi que les budgets de plusieurs institutions, dont la Présidence de la République, la Primature et les juridictions supérieures, n’ont pas obtenu l’approbation des commissaires. Des réserves ont notamment été émises sur la cohérence de certains chiffres et la sincérité des prévisions budgétaires. La séance s’est déroulée sous la présidence d’Alphonse Sambou, président de la Commission, en présence du ministre de l’Économie, des Finances, du Budget et du Plan, Cheikh Diba. Ce dernier était accompagné de Bassirou Sarr, chargé du Budget, et d’Allé Nar Diop, chargé de l’Économie, du Plan et de la Coopération. Les projets présentés portent sur des enveloppes budgétaires d’importance variable selon les institutions. La Présidence de la République se voit ainsi attribuer une dotation de 223,86 milliards de FCFA, contre 204,54 milliards en 2026, soit une hausse de 19,32 milliards. À l’inverse, le budget de l’Assemblée nationale est proposé à 21,11 milliards de FCFA, contre 22,30 milliards l’année précédente. Pour les autres institutions, le projet prévoit 1,50 milliard de FCFA pour le Conseil constitutionnel, 4,69 milliards pour la Cour suprême et 13,07 milliards pour la Cour des comptes. Des réserves sur la sincérité des prévisions Au-delà des montants annoncés, les débats ont surtout porté sur la fiabilité des documents budgétaires soumis aux députés. Plusieurs commissaires ont relevé des incohérences dans certains chiffres et exprimé des interrogations sur la sincérité des prévisions présentées par le Gouvernement. L’absence de certaines pièces justificatives a également suscité des critiques. Des membres de la Commission ont notamment demandé la transmission de la loi de règlement 2025, considérée comme un document nécessaire pour apprécier l’exécution des budgets précédents et mieux examiner les nouvelles propositions. Ces différentes observations ont alimenté les échanges avec les représentants du Gouvernement. Mais elles n’ont pas permis de lever les réserves exprimées par les commissaires. Au terme des discussions, les membres de la Commission des Finances et du Contrôle budgétaire ont voté contre l’ensemble des projets soumis à leur examen, y compris les prévisions de recettes et de dette publique ainsi que les budgets des institutions concernées. C.G. DIOP

items.title: Ziguinchor : l’AIBD « soigne » les riverains et renforce son ancrage local
items.description: Plus de 700 personnes ont bénéficié de consultations médicales gratuites à Lyndiane, à l’initiative de la direction de l’Aéroport international Blaise Diagne (Aibd Sa). Au-delà de cette opération sanitaire, des kits scolaires et des équipements sportifs ont été offerts aux établissements scolaires et aux quatorze ASC des quartiers riverains. ZIGUINCHOR- Le temps d’un week-end, l’AIBD a troqué les pistes aéroportuaires contre les salles de consultation pour aller à la rencontre des populations de Ziguinchor. À l’école Patate de Lyndiane, transformée en centre de soins, médecins et spécialistes ont accueilli des centaines d’habitants venus bénéficier de consultations gratuites et de médicaments. Organisée les 7 et 8 novembre dans le cadre de la politique de Responsabilité sociétale d’entreprise (Rse) de l’AIBD, cette initiative a largement dépassé les prévisions initiales. Plus de 700 personnes ont été consultées, notamment en médecine générale, ophtalmologie et dans le cadre du dépistage de certaines maladies. Pour Cheikh Bamba Dièye, directeur général de l’AIBD Sa, cette démarche traduit une volonté de rapprocher davantage la plateforme aéroportuaire des communautés qui vivent dans son environnement immédiat. « Un aéroport moderne ne doit pas seulement assurer la connectivité entre les territoires. Il doit également entretenir un partenariat solide avec les populations riveraines et contribuer à améliorer leurs conditions de vie », a-t-il souligné. Au-delà de la santé, l'opération a été accompagnée d'une remise de kits scolaires aux établissements bénéficiaires et d'équipements sportifs aux quatorze Associations sportives et culturelles (Asc) des quartiers concernés. Le directeur général de l’AIBD a, par ailleurs, affiché sa volonté d’inscrire ces actions dans la durée. « Nous entendons renouveler et multiplier ces initiatives. La santé, l’éducation, le sport, la culture, mais aussi l’emploi et l’insertion des jeunes resteront au cœur de notre engagement auprès des populations riveraines », a-t-il assuré. Gaustin DIATTA (Correspondant)

items.title: Israeli president picks Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu rival, to try to form government
items.description: Nov 7 (Reuters) - Israel's president on Saturday chose Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's strongest rival, to try to form a new government following a deadlocked election that left neither man with a clear path to power. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader, is fighting to stay in office after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an October 27 election but still emerged as the largest bloc in parliament.

items.title: Tebboune félicite le physicien Noureddine Melikechi
items.description: Le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a félicité ce samedi le physicien algérien Noureddine Melikechi dont le nom sera porté à jamais par un programme de recherche de l’Université du Massachusetts aux États-Unis. « Toutes nos félicitations et notre profonde estime au professeur Noureddine Melikechi, chercheur à la NASA, pour cette distinction scientifique suprême : l'attribution de son nom, à vie, à un programme académique par l’Université du Massachusetts et Monsieur Kennedy. L'Algérie est fière de ce couronnement mérité qui honore votre parcours et votre empreinte en tant que l'un des plus éminents scientifiques de notre époque », a écrit le président de la République dans un message de félicitations publié sur son compte Twitter. Melikechi : « C’est un très grand honneur » M. Melikechi a annoncé vendredi à TSA que l’université de Massachusetts et Monsieur Kennedy ont décidé de donner son nom à vie à un programme de recherche et d’innovation, doté d’un investissement initial de 2,5 millions de dollars. كل التهاني والتقدير، للبروفيسور نورالدين مليكشي، العالم في وكالة « ناسا » على نيله الشرف العلمي السامي، لتسمية أحد البرامج باسمه مدى الحياة، من قبل جامعة ماساشوستس، والسيد كينيدي. تعتز وتفتخر الجزائر كذلك بهذا التتويج لمسيرتك وبصمتك ،كأحد أهم علماء العصر. — عبدالمجيد تبون – Abdelmadjid Tebboune (@TebbouneAmadjid) November 7, 2026 « L’Université du Massachusetts et Monsieur Kennedy ont décidé et annoncé qu’ils créaient un programme qui portera mon nom pour l’éternité. C’est un très grand honneur. Je ne m’y attendais pas, du moins pas de mon vivant », a déclaré le doyen du Kennedy College of Sciences à TSA. L’article Tebboune félicite le physicien Noureddine Melikechi est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 'Please take the job': Trump asks UFC chief Dana White to be White House press secretary
items.description: US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had asked mixed martial ​arts promoter Dana White to serve ‌as White House press secretary and called on him to bring some fighters ​along as assistants “even though some ​are not from our country.” White, chief ⁠executive of the Ultimate Fighting ​Championship, is a “violent Fighter and Warrior,” Trump ​wrote in a Truth Social post. Trump asked for six current or former UFC titleholders to join White, including ​two athletes from Russia’s Dagestan ​region, Islam Makhachev and Khabib Nurmagomedov; Americans Justin ‌Gaethje, ⁠Daniel Cormier and “Kayla Harris,” likely a reference to Kayla Harrison; and Amanda Nunes, a Brazilian native who became ​an ​American citizen ⁠last year. “We need these people to defend us against the ​Lunatic Left,” Trump wrote. White ​and ⁠UFC’s parent company, TKO Group Holdings, did not immediately return requests for comment. Last month, White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia was “let go”, less than a week after she had taken on the role after Trump said he had told her to reconsider the job following public scrutiny. “I told her: ‘I think you’re better off being happy, and I’m not sure you can ever be happy in this stuff.’ There’s nothing easy about this stuff,” Trump told reporters. Zacharia had acknowledged that she had failed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practising law in the United States. She had earlier described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and on social media, and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.

items.title: Hôpital régional de Ziguinchor : une mobilisation pour la propreté
items.description: Au terme de la saison des pluies, de bonnes volontés ont investi ce samedi 07 novembre, le Centre hospitalier régional de Ziguinchor (Chrz) pour une journée intense d’investissement humain en vue de redonner de l’éclat à cet environnement qui accueillit au quotidien, des centaines de patients du Sénégal et de la Guinée-Bissau. ZIGUINCHOR- Mouvements de jeunesse, Associations sportives et culturelles (Asc), groupements de femmes, guides religieux, Croix-Rouge, Agents de sécurité de proximité (Asp) et citoyens se sont mobilisés pour débarrasser la structure sanitaire des herbes et autres déchets accumulés pendant l’hivernage. Balais, râteaux et autres outils d’assainissement à la main, ils ont répondu massivement à l’appel. Au-delà d’une simple opération de nettoyage, cette mobilisation traduit une ambition : faire de l’environnement hospitalier un véritable levier de qualité des soins. Une conviction défendue par Alphouseyni Diatta, chef du service de l’hygiène et de la sécurité de l’établissement sanitaire. S’appuyant sur l’approche « One Health » ou « Une seule santé », qui établit un lien étroit entre la santé humaine, animale et environnementale, il rappelle que la protection de la santé des populations passe nécessairement par un cadre de vie sain. Pour lui, les enseignements de la pandémie de Covid-19 ont suffisamment montré l’interdépendance de ces différentes dimensions. « Il est impossible de parler de soins de qualité sans prendre en compte l’environnement. Un hôpital propre, accueillant et bien entretenu renforce la confiance des patients et leur sentiment de sécurité », a fait remarquer Alphouseyni Diatta. Il plaide ainsi pour une mobilisation permanente afin que l’assainissement ne se limite pas à des opérations ponctuelles. Une responsabilité partagée Cette démarche citoyenne trouve également un écho favorable auprès de Léon Diédhiou, chef du service social du centre hospitalier régional de Ziguinchor. Il souligne l’importance d’une telle initiative au sortir de l’hivernage, période marquée par une forte prolifération de la végétation et des difficultés supplémentaires d’entretien. Selon lui, la réussite de cette journée repose sur la collaboration entre les partenaires, les acteurs communautaires et les guides religieux, dont l’engagement a permis de mobiliser différentes couches de la population. L’objectif est de garantir aux malades et à leurs accompagnants un environnement propre, confortable et respectueux de leur dignité. « En tant qu’établissement de référence, notre devoir est de tout mettre en œuvre pour accueillir les populations dans les meilleures conditions », souligne-t-il. Au nom de la direction et de l’administration, Léon Diédhiou a exprimé sa gratitude à l'ensemble des participants pour leur engagement bénévole. Alphouseyni Diatta a, pour sa part, salué la disponibilité des différentes corporations, notamment les jeunes, les ASP, la Croix-Rouge et les guides religieux. Il a particulièrement magnifié l'implication de Serigne Dame Dieng, dont la capacité à mobiliser les fidèles constitue un précieux atout pour la réussite de cette initiative. À Ziguinchor, cette journée a ainsi dépassé le simple cadre de l'assainissement. Elle a surtout démontré que l'hôpital n'est pas seulement l'affaire des soignants et de l'administration. Sa propreté, son attractivité et la qualité de son accueil sont aussi une responsabilité collective, au bénéfice de tous les usagers. Gaustin DIATTA (Correspondant)

items.title: Eisenkot to be tasked with forming next Israeli government
items.description: In a setback to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, his main rival will be tasked with forming the next Israeli government, placing him one step closer to ousting Israel’s longest-serving leader, even as the path remains complicated. Gadi Eisenkot, a retired military chief who led the centrist Yashar party in the October 27 election, will have up to six weeks to try and assemble a coalition to replace Netanyahu. But his path to power is fraught with political obstacles and divisions within the opposition itself. President Isaac Herzog will officially give Eisenkot the mandate to form a government on Sunday, his office said in a statement. Herzog’s decision followed two days of consultations last week with all parties elected to the Knesset. Eisenkot secured the support of 67 members of the incoming Knesset, including 19 from the two Arab parties. Netanyahu received just 46 recommendations. A notable crack in his once-loyal bloc was exposed during the consultations when United Torah Judaism, a traditional Netanyahu ally, declined to recommend him. Yet Herzog’s decision does not automatically remove Netanyahu from power. Eisenkot has a mandate and a parliamentary majority on paper, but not yet a governing coalition. Eisenkot is pushing to form what he calls a “national emergency government” and to swear in a minority government as soon as possible. It would comprise the four Jewish opposition parties, which together hold 48 seats: his own Yashar; Together, led by former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid; Avigdor Liberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu, and the left-wing Democrats, led by Yair Golan. He has set four conditions for joining: recognizing Israel as a Jewish, democratic, liberal, and egalitarian state, commitment to the values of the Declaration of Independence, universal service – whether military, national, or civilian – and recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organization. Palestinian candidate Yousef Jabareen of the Joint List party reacts to exit polls during Israel’s national election, at the party election headquarters in Nazareth, northern Israel, on October 27, 2026. Jamal Awad/Reuters The last condition effectively rules out the Arab parties from sitting in the Cabinet. But they could still support the government from outside, providing a parliamentary safety net. Israeli law requires only a simple majority to establish a government. Removing one is far more difficult, requires an absolute majority of 61 votes who support an alternative government. (The Knesset has 120 seats.) Eisenkot’s central obstacle is Avigdor Liberman. The Yisrael Beitenu leader and, at different times, former defense, foreign affairs and finance minister, has ruled out any government dependent on the Arab parties. A minority government, he argues, will be short-lived, and in the long run, will only strengthen Netanyahu. “We’ll have Netanyahu come back with 70 seats for another four years, and from there it’s a short road to annihilation,” Liberman wrote on X on Friday. Avigdor Lieberman, head of the Yisrael Beiteinu party, has emerged as a stubborn obstacle to Eisenkot forming a government with the help of Arab parties. Jack Guez/AFP/Getty Images Instead, Liberman proposed a different route. Dropping his years-long veto on the ultra-Orthodox parties, he urged to make a “maximum effort” to form a coalition of 61 lawmakers with the two ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism, and without the Joint List and Ra’am. Once it is formed, he added, three or four lawmakers from the Likud may defect. That plan, however, clashes with one of the opposition’s core commitments: to end the blanket draft exemption for ultra-Orthodox men from mandatory military service. The ultra-Orthodox parties are pressing for legislation that would enshrine the exemption, and Eisenkot, Liberman and the rest of the opposition pledged universal service throughout the campaign. Moreover, one of the ultra-Orthodox parties remains loyal to Netanyahu. Netanyahu, who lost his parliamentary majority, is also applying heavy pressure against any Jewish-Arab political cooperation. He is challenging the election results and claims the vote was “stolen” by Arab parties by bribery and foreign funding. David Zini, his loyalist Shin Bet director, has been pushing to investigate Arab politicians without any public evidence. In a video statement Saturday, Netanyahu warned that if a minority government is formed with the Arab parties’ support, Israel will “simply not survive.” Instead, he called for a national unity government with his entire bloc, which includes far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties. Netanyahu called for “all Zionist parties that want to preserve our one and only state of the Jewish people.” Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gestures to his supporters at the election night rally after the first exit polls were announced. Jalaa Marey/AFP/Getty Images Eisenkot dismissed his message as a “pathetic spin.” In a statement, the Yashar party said, “If the Likud wants a broad unity government, it is more than welcome to announce the dissolution of the alliance with the extremists and enter a government under Prime Minister Eisenkot.” Eisenkot’s first test comes Tuesday with the swearing in of the new Knesset. The opposition intends to replace Netanyahu’s Knesset speaker, weakening his grip on power and allowing the opposition parties to begin taking some actions, such as forming a state commission of inquiry into the security failures that led to the October 7, 2023, attack by Hamas. Starting Sunday, Eisenkot will have 28 days to negotiate with other parties over Cabinet posts, budgets and policies, with a possible 14-day extension. If he fails, the mandate passes to Netanyahu for another four weeks. Eisenkot said on Friday he intends to form a government as quickly as possible, framing the moment as a national emergency. “A situation in which a caretaker prime minister in the minority, who has lost the trust of the people in such an extreme way, continues to operate the security system and law enforcement authorities, is a dangerous situation that must not continue even for one more day,” he wrote on X.

items.title: La Fédération égyptienne de football officialise le divorce avec Hossam Hassan
items.description: Clap de fin brutal pour Hossam Hassan à la tête de la sélection égyptienne. La rumeur circulait depuis quelques jours, c'est maintenant officiel. Fédération égyptienne de football (EFA) a officialisé, ce samedi 7 novembre, le limogeage du technicien de 60 ans et de l'ensemble de son encadrement technique et administratif, à seulement deux jours du début du rassemblement des Pharaons. Dans la foulée, l'instance fédérale a annoncé la nomination immédiate d'Ali Maher pour lui succéder sur le banc, avec pour première mission la double confrontation face au Malawi, prévue les 13 et 17 novembre dans le cadre des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. La décision a été entérinée lors de la réunion du comité exécutif de l'EFA, qui a invoqué la préservation de l'image de la sélection nationale pour justifier cette rupture contractuelle. « À la suite de sa réunion (…), et après avoir examiné l’ensemble des circonstances et des événements survenus ces derniers temps, ainsi que leurs répercussions et leur impact négatif sur l’image positive de notre équipe nationale et sur sa stabilité, le Conseil d’administration a décidé, dans le cadre de ses responsabilités, de remercier le sélectionneur Hossam Hassan ainsi que son staff technique et administratif, conformément aux clauses du contrat » , précise le communiqué officiel. Ce dénouement intervient dans un climat de vive controverse extrasportive. Depuis le parcours des Pharaons jusqu'en huitièmes de finale du Mondial 2026 face à l'Argentine, Hossam Hassan se retrouvait au cœur d'un déballage médiatique persistant lié à des querelles publiques avec ses deux ex-épouses. Malgré les avertissements répétés de la fédération l'enjoignant à préserver sa vie privée pour se concentrer sur ses fonctions, la diffusion de clichés compromettants a précipité la rupture avec les instances dirigeantes. La situation s'était encore détériorée avec une interdiction formelle de toute apparition publique infligée à l'ancien international par le Conseil suprême de régulation des médias pour atteinte à la vie privée — une mesure rendant concrètement impossible la tenue de ses conférences de presse et l'annonce de ses listes de convoqués. Face à la grogne grandissante des cadres du vestiaire, aux condamnations d'anciennes gloires du football national et à l'indignation d'organisations de défense des droits des femmes, la Fédération égyptienne a choisi de trancher dans le vif afin de restaurer la stabilité des Pharaons avant les prochaines échéances continentales. The post La Fédération égyptienne de football officialise le divorce avec Hossam Hassan appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Climat et santé: les six mesures OMS qui pourraient éviter 1,6 million de décès par an
items.description: Six mesures éprouvées de lutte contre le changement climatique pourraient permettre d'éviter 1,6 million de décès par an dans le monde et générer chaque année 3.900 milliards de dollars de bénéfices économiques ainsi que 5.400 milliards de dollars de recettes budgétaires supplémentaires, selon un rapport publié mercredi par l'Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS). Intitulée “Global benefits and costs of prioritized actions on climate change and health”, cette étude évalue pour la première fois les retombées économiques et financières d'une généralisation de six interventions recommandées par l'organisation. Celles-ci comprennent les systèmes d'alerte sanitaire face aux fortes chaleurs, l'accès à des services d'approvisionnement en eau potable résilients au changement climatique, l'assainissement de base, les installations d'hygiène et de lavage des mains, le recours à des combustibles et technologies plus propres pour la cuisson et le chauffage domestiques, ainsi que des politiques efficaces de tarification des combustibles fossiles. Leur mise en œuvre à l'échelle mondiale pourrait également permettre d'éviter l'émission de 16,7 milliards de tonnes de CO₂, soit l'équivalent de 31% des émissions annuelles mondiales de gaz à effet de serre, hors utilisation des terres, changement d'affectation des terres et foresterie, estime l'OMS. Selon les projections modélisées, les décès évités représenteraient un décès sur 40 à l'échelle mondiale. Parmi les mesures étudiées, les politiques de tarification des combustibles fossiles, notamment la suppression des subventions inefficaces et une taxation appropriée, offriraient les retombées les plus importantes. Elles pourraient à elles seules prévenir 1,2 million de décès par an et générer 3.000 milliards de dollars de bénéfices économiques ainsi que 5.400 milliards de dollars de recettes publiques supplémentaires. Les systèmes d'alerte sanitaire en cas de fortes chaleurs figurent également parmi les interventions les plus rentables, avec un rendement estimé à 835 dollars de bénéfices pour chaque dollar investi. Pour cinq des six mesures évaluées, chaque dollar investi rapporterait en moyenne 24 dollars de bénéfices, selon le rapport. Les gains seraient particulièrement importants dans les pays à revenu faible ou intermédiaire, contribuant ainsi à réduire les inégalités sanitaires et économiques. “La crise climatique est une crise sanitaire, mais une grande partie des dommages qu'elle provoque peut être évitée grâce à des outils dont nous disposons déjà”, a déclaré le directeur général de l'OMS, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, appelant les gouvernements à placer la protection de la santé au cœur de leurs politiques climatiques. Publiée à l'approche de la COP31, où les gouvernements doivent présenter leurs engagements climatiques, l'étude appelle à renforcer les investissements dans des mesures permettant d'anticiper, de prévenir et de limiter les risques sanitaires liés au dérèglement climatique. L'analyse de l'OMS porte sur la période 2024-2075 et compare des scénarios de généralisation des interventions à des scénarios sans extension de leur couverture. L'organisation souligne toutefois que les résultats reposent sur des projections à long terme, des scénarios de déploiement ambitieux et des bases de données encore limitées, ce qui comporte des incertitudes. items.description: Le chef du bloc de l'opposition au Premier ministre sortant, Benjamin Netanyahu, Gadi Eisenkot, sera chargé dimanche de de former le gouvernement israélien, a indiqué samedi soir la présidence. « Le président Herzog a invité Gadi Eizenkot à la résidence présidentielle, où il lui confiera demain, à 17H00, la mission de former le gouvernement », selon le communiqué. items.title: BERD : l’agriculture hisse la croissance marocaine à 4,8 %
items.description: Révisées en hausse de 0,4 point depuis juin, les prévisions de la Banque européenne pour la reconstruction et le développement tablent sur une croissance de 4,8 % en 2026, portée par le rebond agricole, avant un tassement à 3,9 % en 2027. Dans la dernière édition de ses Perspectives économiques régionales, arrêtée au 14 septembre 2026, la BERD relève la projection de croissance du Royaume pour cette année, alors que l’économie nationale affiche une trajectoire en nette amélioration. Le produit intérieur brut avait progressé de 3,8 % en 2024, puis de 4,9 % en 2025. Pour 2027, l’institution abaisse légèrement son estimation, de 0,1 point, à 3,9 %. Ce relèvement tranche avec le tableau d’ensemble de la région sud et est de la Méditerranée, dont la croissance devrait ressortir à -0,7 % en 2026. La moyenne régionale est tirée vers le bas par la récession en Irak, où les exportations pétrolières ont été fortement perturbées par la fermeture du détroit d’Ormuz, dans le sillage du conflit déclenché au Moyen-Orient le 28 février 2026, ainsi que par la situation du Liban. Hors Irak, la zone devrait croître de 3,9 % cette année puis de 4,3 % en 2027. Avec 4,8 %, le Maroc devance l’Égypte (4,6 %), la Jordanie (2,5 %) et la Tunisie (2,4 %), même si Le Caire est attendu plus haut en 2027, à 5 %. La BERD indique avoir revu à la hausse les prévisions pour le Maroc et la Tunisie en raison de la vigueur de la production agricole. Au premier trimestre 2026, la croissance s’est établie à 4,6 % en glissement annuel, contre 5,0 % un an plus tôt, l’investissement ayant ralenti après avoir atteint un niveau exceptionnellement élevé. La reprise de l’agriculture, consécutive à plusieurs années de sécheresse, s’est poursuivie, avec une production en hausse de 18,4 %. Ce regain a compensé un fléchissement de l’activité dans l’industrie et la construction. Pour l’ensemble du premier semestre, la BERD retient une estimation non officielle de 4,6 %. L’inflation est restée très contenue, avec une moyenne de 0,5 % sur les six premiers mois de l’année, en dépit d’une accélération passagère liée au renchérissement de l’énergie. Dans ce contexte, Bank Al-Maghrib a maintenu son taux directeur à 2,25 % en juin dernier, pour la cinquième fois consécutive, en invoquant le niveau élevé des incertitudes géopolitiques. Sur le plan budgétaire, le gouvernement table sur un déficit de 3,4 % du PIB en 2026, conforme à l’objectif fixé par la loi de finances, et sur un ratio d’endettement ramené à 65,8 % du PIB, contre 66,6 % en 2025. Les marchés ont, de leur côté, réservé un bon accueil au pays : l’émission obligataire internationale de mai 2026 a été sursouscrite. Les comptes extérieurs affichent également une bonne tenue. Le déficit courant s’est limité à 1,2 % du PIB au premier trimestre, l’élargissement du déficit commercial ayant été compensé par les recettes touristiques et les transferts des Marocains du monde, qualifiés de solides. Les réserves officielles de change se sont élevées à 54,3 milliards de dollars en août 2026, soit environ 5,3 mois d’importations. Dans ses scénarios, la BERD identifie deux principaux facteurs de risque pour la trajectoire marocaine : la volatilité des cours des matières premières et l’incertitude entourant la politique commerciale à l’échelle mondiale. L’institution relève à ce propos que les droits de douane américains ont été modifiés à plusieurs reprises en juillet 2026, dans un contexte où l’énergie reste soumise à de fortes tensions, le Brent s’étant maintenu au-dessus de 100 dollars le baril à la mi-septembre. The post BERD : l’agriculture hisse la croissance marocaine à 4,8 % appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Clashes erupt in Paris amid new protests across France
items.description: Thousands of people protested across France on Saturday in a new show of anger against the government, with clashes erupting between police and some protesters in Paris despite a lower turnout than in previous weeks. The protests marked the fourth consecutive weekend of demonstrations against the rising cost of living, which have erupted as the country heads to presidential elections in five months’ time, where the far right sees its best chance yet to win power. A total of 146,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Saturday, including 46,000 in Paris, the interior ministry said. Unions put the figure at 250,000 protesters nationwide, with 75,000 in the capital. A protestor runs through tear gas during a demonstration in Paris on November 7, 2026. — AFP These figures were lower than the previous three weekends of protests but also came after a mass union protest on Thursday that rallied 575,000 people, according to the authorities — 1.6 million according to unions. At the end of the protest in Paris, police used tear gas against individuals throwing projectiles and homemade fireworks at the security forces, an AFP correspondent said. Police said a group of 200 violent individuals attacked officers as they were arresting a man who had set fire to a trash bin in the square. Banned protests thwarted Some 70,000 members of the security forces were deployed on Saturday, ready to move in quickly after mass protests on October 17 degenerated into the worst riots seen in France in years. Unions had staged a march along a traditional route, from the Place de la Republique in central Paris to Place de la Nation in the east of the city where the clashes erupted at the end of the protest. But the Yellow Vests movement — a group whose protests shook Emmanuel Macron in the early years of his presidency almost a decade ago — called for a rival demonstration at the Place de la Concorde in central Paris, a stone’s throw from the president’s Élysée Palace and the lower house of parliament. This action has been banned by the authorities, and on Saturday a large police presence prevented protesters from getting close. Some 100 people who arrived were surrounded by police and one of the movement’s coordinators, Benjamin Ball, and its spokeswoman, Azelma Sigaux, were among those arrested by police, an AFP reporter said. In the southeastern city of Lyon, police fired tear gas to disperse several hundred people in the city centre blocking a road during an unauthorised gathering. ‘This can’t go on’ The wave of demonstrations was sparked by a movement in late September by high school students angered by conditions at their establishments. These teens, joined by university students, remain at the heart of the protests. “Today is a date that helps keep the pressure on,” said Sabine Kharbach, spokeswoman of the Student Union. “Many young people are mobilising because the government’s responses remain unsatisfactory.” The police response has faced criticism for being heavy-handed, with dozens of internal investigations launched into allegations of brutality against demonstrators. A protestor shoots fireworks during a demonstration in Paris, France on November 7, 2026. — AFP Local businesses are also feeling the pain. “So this can’t go on, otherwise I think it will be a disaster before long,” said Paris shop manager Jean Emile Moulinier. His store is around the main protest route and he said hardly any customers brave security barricades on protest weekends. Shop windows of stores in Paris and other cities were again barricaded with wooden shutters and often closed for the day to prevent potential ransacking. The government is grappling with ways to find solutions but is constrained by France’s gigantic debt pile, which is already spooking markets. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is to meet unions and employer federation representatives on Monday to discuss wages and purchasing power. But student and teacher groups in France have called for a new strike on Tuesday to keep pressure on the government for more education spending, saying they were “in a position of strength [and] the government in a position of weakness and starting to yield”. Polls indicate that far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the favourite to win the Elysee in 2027, with her main rival currently not one of Macron’s centrist former allies but hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon. Melenchon, addressing 20,000 at a rally outside Paris on Saturday, declared “we are going to win” and “everything must change”.

items.title: CM Bugti's remarks about FWO's performance taken out of context: Balochistan minister
items.description: GWADAR: Balochistan Planning Minister Mir Zahoor Ahmad Buledi has said Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti’s recent remarks regarding the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) had been presented out of context. Buledi’s clarification comes over a week after CM Bugti acknowledged shortcomings in FWO’s performance while responding to remarks made by National Party leader Dr Abdul Malik Baloch, who had also criticised the entity. Speaking on a point of order in the Balochistan Assembly in late October, Baloch, a former chief minister, had criticised the contracting process for road projects and alleged that the FWO had awarded work according to its own preferences. In reply, CM Bugti expressed his dissatisfaction with the FWO’s performance, adding that the elected provincial assembly shared these concerns. The chief minister said even roads constructed in his own area had deteriorated. He said the organisation was awarded projects with the expectation of quality work, but claimed that the entity handed projects to smaller subcontractors, resulting in poor execution. Regarding projects by the National Highways Authority (NHA), Bugti said security-related challenges also affec­ted some road schemes and that the government was addressing those issues. On Friday, addressing an informal dialogue programme at the Turbat Press Club auditorium, Buledi emphasised that the FWO had rendered invaluable services for the construction of highways in Balochistan. He recalled that multiple personnel had lost their lives during the construction of the Hoshab-Panjgur-Surab Highway (N-85). Buledi also highlighted the Balochistan government’s efforts to prioritise infrastructure development, education, healthcare and youth employment. Reiterating his position on the broader situation and development agenda in Balochistan, Buledi defended the FWO, terming its overall performance in the province commendable. Criticising certain political opponents, the PPP leader claimed they opposed the province’s progress and had attempted to create negative narratives around infrastructure projects. He cited their opposition to the Hub Industrial Zone, Gwadar Port, Mirani Dam, Gishkor Dam, and the South Balochistan Package , accusing them of misleading the public for political gain despite these initiatives being vital for regional prosperity. In August, a high-level meeting of the Communication and Works (C&W) Department reviewed progress on Phase I and II of road-sector projects launched across the province under the Balochistan Socio-Economic Development Programme. Chairing the meeting, C&W Secretary Babar Khan expressed dissatisfaction over the slow pace of work on certain critical projects.

items.title: Gov’t allocates GH¢250M in 2027 budget for completion of Blekusu Coastal Protection Project
items.description: President John Mahama has announced an additional GH¢250 million allocation in the 2027 budget for the continuation and completion of the Blekusu Phase Two Coastal Protection Project. The President said the funding is intended to ensure the uninterrupted execution of the project intended to deal with the severity of coastal erosion in the area. Addressing the 2026 Hogbetsotso Festival, President Mahama said the additional allocation is in response to appeals by traditional leaders and residents for the project to be completed. “I have also heard your appeal for the uninterrupted continuation and completion of the Blekusu Phase Two Coastal Protection Project,” he said. “I wish to announce to you that I am happy with the progress of WACA, and I am pleased to inform you that an additional amount of GH¢250 million has been allocated in the 2027 Budget for the continuation and completion of the Blekusu Phase Two Project.” The announcement comes amid concerns about the impact of coastal erosion on communities along Ghana’s coastline, particularly homes, fishing livelihoods, schools and other community infrastructure. The Blekusu Phase Two project is expected to protect an eight-kilometre stretch of coastline, covering Blekusu, Agavedzi, Salakope, Amutsinu and Adina in the Ketu South Municipality of the Volta Region. The project was officially launched in July 2025 and is designed to protect the five communities from persistent tidal waves and coastal erosion, which have destroyed homes, displaced residents and threatened livelihoods over the years. It involves the construction of 37 groynes, reinforced embankments and dune restoration works. Additional facilities, including a modern fish market, cold storage and fish processing facilities, are also part of the development plan. The project is being undertaken by Amandi Holdings Limited. Beyond the Blekusu project, President Mahama announced that GH¢685 million has been allocated to commence coastal protection interventions under the West African Coastal Areas Resilience Investment Project (WACA). He said the funding would support a combination of engineering and environmental interventions to address coastal erosion and protect vulnerable communities. The President added that the project would also involve lagoon and watershed rehabilitation, alongside livelihood support for communities within the targeted programme areas, particularly young people, women and persons with disabilities. WACA is a coastal resilience programme designed to address erosion, flooding, pollution and environmental degradation along vulnerable coastal areas. It combines physical infrastructure with environmental restoration and community-level interventions. President Mahama also called on traditional authorities and residents to support efforts to protect mangroves and wetlands, warning that their destruction weakens the shoreline and increases the vulnerability of coastal communities. “It is a known fact that the unrestricted destruction of mangroves and coastal vegetation weakens our shoreline and leaves our coast vulnerable to erosion,” he said. He urged residents to support the protection of the natural environment as part of efforts to safeguard coastal settlements.

items.title: Ghana to host 2027 Karting Africa Showrun
items.description: Ghana has been awarded the hosting rights for the 2027 edition of the Karting Africa Showrun, with the event scheduled to take place at the Independence Square in Accra next December. The competition, which will be staged for the fifth time, is expected to attract approximately 60 drivers from 20 countries. President of the Ghana Motorsport Federation, Kwabena Poku, exclusively confirmed the development to JoySports, describing it as a major opportunity for Ghana to showcase its motorsport potential. “Ghana has actually gotten the bid and rights to host the Karting Africa series in Ghana next year in December. We’re bringing about 20 countries to Accra to compete at the Independence Square, with about 60 drivers from about 20 countries who will be racing proper racing karts in Accra,” he said. Ghana’s successful bid comes after the country made its mark on the African motorsport stage at this year’s edition in Benguela, Angola, where a three-driver team made history with its participation. The outing marked a significant milestone for Ghanaian motorsport, with the team competing against some of the continent’s finest young racing talents and showcasing the country’s growing ambitions in karting. Hosting the 2027 event is expected to build on that progress, providing further opportunities for young Ghanaian drivers and strengthening efforts to develop motorsport locally. Interested drivers can register through the official Karting Africa website, www.kartingafrica.com .

items.title: Sidi Bouzid | Enquête sanitaire suite à l’intoxication de 22 élèves du lycée pilote
items.description: Une enquête a été ouverte suite à l'intoxication de 22 élèves du lycée pilote de Sidi Bouzid, transférés dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi à l’hôpital universitaire de la région. Ces derniers ont manifesté des symptômes évocateurs d'une intoxication alimentaire, notamment des vertiges, des vomissements et de violentes douleurs abdominales, indique une source médicale à l'agence TAP. La même source précise que l'intervention rapide des secours et du personnel soignant a permis d'administrer les traitements nécessaires dès leur admission. Face à cet incident, les services d’hygiène de la région ont immédiatement diligenté des investigations sur le terrain. Des prélèvements conservatoires ont été effectués sur les composants du repas servi au réfectoire de l'établissement scolaire afin d'être soumis à des analyses microbiologiques poussées en laboratoire pour déterminer l'origine exacte des troubles. Y. N. L’article Sidi Bouzid | Enquête sanitaire suite à l'intoxication de 22 élèves du lycée pilote est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election
items.description: There was no clear winner following New Zealand’s election on Saturday, as the leaders of its two major parties preparing for negotiations to form a coalition government. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s centre-right National Party won 42 seats but was 19 short of the simple majority needed to form a government, despite being the largest party, preliminary results show. Combined with their coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First, they would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc if a deal could be reached. But opposition leader Chris Hipkins, whose Labour Party won 36seats, showed no signs of conceding, saying the “shape of the next government” will remain uncertain “for a while”. The tight result followed a campaign shaped by the cost of living and unemployment. Projections show the National Party on 42 seats and Labour on 36. The Greens are on 16, with ACT on 13, New Zealand First on 12, the Opportunity Party on 7 and Te Pāti Māori, which represents Māori interests, on 5. The electoral commission was not due to announced the official result until 27 November. Luxon congratulated Hipkins on a “very hard-fought race” before addressing party colleagues, saying “whatever the final count, we are incredibly proud of each and everyone for you”. He said he would run a caretaker government until the final results were confirmed later in the month, adding: “With those final results there can then be meaningful negotiations.” Elsewhere, Labour leader Kipkins said “the people have spoken”, adding: “It may take a bit longer to work out what they’ve said.” Hipkins said the results made clear the “next parliament is going to require all of us to compromise, to work together and to find a common ground”. More than 99% of votes have been counted in New Zealand, with National and Labour neck-and-neck in terms of vote share. But the preliminary results pointed to historically low support for the two major parties, with a combined vote share of around 60%. They were followed by the Greens, ACT, New Zealand First, centrist party Opportunity and Te Pāti Māori, which represents Māori interests. The Opportunity Party crossed the 5% threshold to enter parliament for the first time, with leader Qiulae Wong saying would work with either side. It has been described as this election’s kingmaker as it remains open to working with either major bloc, but its leaders said they would negotiate first with the party that secures the most seats. Speaking at Opportunity’s watch party, Wong told supporters: “We believe that we can change the way we do politics to focus on the future, on the next generation, and on finding common ground.” Professor Andrew Geddis from the University of Otago, an expert in election law, said “the Opportunity Party as a wildcard player” could “determine which bloc of parties is able to govern”. “It will come down to some very fine vote margins not just between the parties, but in individual electorates. We are going to have to wait for the special votes to be processed and counted over the next three weeks,” he said. Special votes are votes cast outside a voter’s electorate, including overseas. The Greens – who have proposed forcing the country’s two main supermarkets to divest stores to create publicly-owned shops – saw their vote rise by a couple of percentage points. Julian McCrann, head of polling at Roy Morgan, told BBC News the cost of living was the main issue for many New Zealanders “Three years ago, Luxon came in saying he’d be making New Zealanders’ lives better and solving these economic issues, but he hasn’t really delivered,” he said. More than half of the country no longer see New Zealand as a land of opportunity, according to an annual social cohesion survey. Record numbers of Kiwis have been leaving the country, with many going to Australia. New Zealand’s mixed-member proportional voting system means most governments are coalitions. Each voter makes two choices – for the representative of their constituency in parliament and a political party.
